sentences.zh: 【後唐紀一】 昭陽協洽，一年。

translations.literal: [Later Tang Records 1] Zhaoyang Xieqia; one year in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Later Tang Records 1] Zhaoyang Xieqia—one year in all.

sentences.zh: 莊宗光聖神閔孝皇帝上同光元年（

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong Guangsheng Shenmin Xiaoxiao, first part—first year of Tongguang (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuangzong Guangsheng Shenmin Xiaoxiao, first part—first year of Tongguang (

sentences.zh: 癸未，公元九二三年）

translations.literal: guiwei, CE 923)
translations.idiomatic: guiwei, 923 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，二月，晉王下教置百官，於四鎮判官中選前朝士族，欲以為相。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, the Prince of Jin issued an order to establish the full bureaucracy; from among the military commissioners' judges of the four circuits he selected former-dynasty gentry families, intending to make them chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the second month, the Prince of Jin ordered the establishment of a full bureaucracy and, from among the judges of the four circuits, chose men from former-dynasty gentry families to serve as chancellors.

sentences.zh: 河東節度判官盧質為之首，質固辭，請以義武節度判官豆盧革、河東觀察判官盧程為之；

translations.literal: Lu Zhi, judge of the Hedong military commission, was placed first; Zhi firmly declined and asked that Doulu Ge, judge of the Yiwu military commission, and Lu Cheng, judge of the Hedong observation commission, be appointed instead;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi of the Hedong commission was named first, but he firmly declined and recommended Doulu Ge of Yiwu and Lu Cheng of Hedong instead;

sentences.zh: 王即召革、程拜行台左、右丞相，以質為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: the Prince at once summoned Ge and Cheng and appointed them left and right chancellors of the provisional government, making Zhi Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince immediately summoned Ge and Cheng and appointed them left and right chancellors of the provisional government, while naming Zhi Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 梁主遣兵部侍郎崔協等冊命吳越王鏐為吳越國王。

translations.literal: The Liang emperor sent Vice Minister of War Cui Xie and others to invest King Qian Liu of Wuyue as King of the State of Wuyue.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor dispatched Vice Minister of War Cui Xie and others to invest Qian Liu of Wuyue as king of the state of Wuyue.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，鏐始建國，儀衛名稱多如天子之制，謂所居曰宮殿，府署曰朝廷，教令下統內曰制敕，將吏皆稱臣，惟不改元，表疏稱吳越國而不言軍。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Liu first established his state; ceremonial guard and titles largely followed the Son of Heaven's model—his residence was called a palace, government offices the court, orders issued within his domain imperial edicts, and officers and clerks all styled themselves subjects; only the era name was not changed, and memorials referred to the State of Wuyue without mentioning the military commission.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Qian Liu formally founded his state. Ceremonial guard and titles largely mirrored those of an emperor: his residence was called a palace, his offices the court, and his orders to the realm imperial edicts; officers and clerks all styled themselves subjects. Only the era name went unchanged, and memorials spoke of the state of Wuyue rather than the military commission.

sentences.zh: 以清海節度使兼侍中傳瓘為鎮海、鎮東留後，總軍府事。

translations.literal: He made Fu Jin, military commissioner of Qinghai and concurrent Palace Attendant, acting commissioner of Zhenhai and Zhendong to oversee military headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Fu Jin, military commissioner of Qinghai and concurrent Palace Attendant, acting commissioner of Zhenhai and Zhendong to oversee military headquarters affairs.

sentences.zh: 置百官，有丞相、侍郎、郎中、員外郎、客省等使。

translations.literal: He established a full bureaucracy, with chancellors, vice ministers, bureau directors, bureau vice directors, and commissioners such as the Guest Reception commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He established a full bureaucracy, including chancellors, vice ministers, bureau directors, bureau vice directors, and commissioners such as the guest reception commissioner.

sentences.zh: 李繼韜雖受晉王命為安義留後，終不自安，幕僚魏琢、牙將申蒙復從而間之曰：「晉朝無人，終為梁所並耳。」

translations.literal: Although Li Jiyao had received the Prince of Jin's appointment as acting commissioner of Anyi, he never felt secure; staff adviser Wei Zhuo and guard officer Shen Mengfu again played on his fears, saying, "The Jin court has no capable men and will in the end be swallowed by Liang."
translations.idiomatic: Although Li Jiyao had accepted the Prince of Jin's appointment as acting commissioner of Anyi, he never felt secure. His staff adviser Wei Zhuo and guard officer Shen Mengfu again played on his fears, saying, "The Jin court has no capable leaders and will in the end be swallowed up by Liang."

sentences.zh: 會晉王置百官，三月，召監軍張居翰、節度判官任圜赴魏州，琢、蒙復說繼韜曰：「王急召二人，情可知矣。」

translations.literal: Just then the Prince of Jin established the bureaucracy; in the third month he summoned army supervisor Zhang Juhan and commission judge Ren Yuan to Weizhou. Zhuo and Mengfu said to Jiyao, "The Prince's urgent summons to these two men—his intent is obvious."
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Prince of Jin established his bureaucracy. In the third month he urgently summoned army supervisor Zhang Juhan and commission judge Ren Yuan to Weizhou. Zhuo and Mengfu told Jiyao, "The Prince's urgent summons to these two men—his intent is obvious."

sentences.zh: 繼韜弟繼遠亦勸繼韜自托於梁，繼韜乃使繼遠詣大梁，請以澤潞為梁臣。

translations.literal: Jiyao's younger brother Jiyuan also urged Jiyao to place himself under Liang's protection, and Jiyao therefore sent Jiyuan to Daliang to request that Ze and Lu submit to Liang as subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyao's younger brother Jiyuan also urged him to throw in his lot with Liang, so Jiyao sent Jiyuan to Daliang to offer Ze and Lu as Liang subjects.

sentences.zh: 梁主大喜，更命安義軍曰匡義，以繼韜為節度使、同平章事。

translations.literal: The Liang emperor was greatly pleased, renamed the Anyi army the Kuangyi army, and appointed Jiyao military commissioner and concurrent Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor was delighted. He renamed the Anyi army the Kuangyi army and appointed Jiyao military commissioner and concurrent Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 繼韜以二子為質。

translations.literal: Jiyao sent two sons as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyao sent two sons to Liang as hostages.

sentences.zh: 安義舊將裴約戍澤州，泣諭其眾曰：「餘事故使逾二紀，見其分財享士，志滅仇讎。

translations.literal: Pei Yue, a veteran officer of Anyi garrisoning Ze Prefecture, addressed his troops in tears: "I have served the late commissioner for more than twenty years and have seen him share wealth with his men and resolve to destroy his enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yue, a veteran Anyi officer garrisoning Ze Prefecture, addressed his troops in tears: "I have served the late commissioner for more than twenty years and watched him share his wealth with his men and set his heart on destroying his enemies.

sentences.zh: 不幸捐館，柩猶未葬，而郎君遽背君親，吾寧死不能從也！」

translations.literal: He has unfortunately died, and his coffin is not yet buried, yet the young lord has abruptly turned against his sovereign and kin—I would rather die than follow him!"
translations.idiomatic: He has died before his time, and his coffin is not yet buried, yet the young lord has abruptly betrayed his sovereign and kin—I would rather die than follow him!"

sentences.zh: 遂據州自守。

translations.literal: He then seized the prefecture and held it on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: He then seized the prefecture and held it on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 梁主以其驍將董璋為澤州刺史，將兵攻之。

translations.literal: The Liang emperor appointed his fierce general Dong Zhang prefect of Ze and sent troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor appointed his fierce general Dong Zhang prefect of Ze and sent troops to attack him.

sentences.zh: 繼韜散財募士，堯山人郭威往應募。

translations.literal: Jiyao distributed wealth to recruit soldiers; Guo Wei of Yaoshan went to enlist.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyao distributed wealth to recruit soldiers, and Guo Wei of Yaoshan came to enlist.

sentences.zh: 威使氣殺人，繫獄，繼韜惜其才勇而逸之。

translations.literal: Wei, in a fit of temper, killed a man and was imprisoned; Jiyao valued his talent and courage and released him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei had killed a man in a fit of temper and was imprisoned, but Jiyao valued his talent and courage and released him.

sentences.zh: 契丹寇幽州，晉王問帥子郭崇韜，崇韜薦橫海節度使李存審。

translations.literal: The Khitan raided You Prefecture; the Prince of Jin asked his chief strategist Guo Chongtao, and Chongtao recommended Li Cunshen, military commissioner of Henghai.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan raided You Prefecture, the Prince of Jin asked his chief strategist Guo Chongtao, who recommended Li Cunshen, military commissioner of Henghai.

sentences.zh: 時存審臥病，己卯，徙存審為盧龍節度使，輿疾赴鎮，以蕃漢馬步副總管李嗣源領橫海節度使。

translations.literal: Cunshen was then bedridden with illness; on jimao he was transferred to military commissioner of Lulong and went to his post despite sickness in a litter, while Li Siyuan, deputy overall commander of Khitan and Han horse and foot, took charge of the Henghai commission.
translations.idiomatic: Cunshen was then bedridden. On jimao he was transferred to military commissioner of Lulong and went to his post despite illness in a litter, while Li Siyuan, deputy overall commander of Khitan and Han horse and foot, took over the Henghai commission.

sentences.zh: 晉王築壇於魏州牙城之南，夏，四月，己巳，升壇，祭告上帝，遂即皇帝位，國號大唐，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin built an altar south of the Weizhou headquarters compound; in summer, the fourth month, on jisi he ascended the altar, offered sacrifice and announced it to High Heaven, and thereupon assumed the imperial throne; the state was named Great Tang, a general amnesty was proclaimed, and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin built an altar south of the Weizhou headquarters. In summer, the fourth month, on jisi he ascended it, sacrificed and announced his accession to Heaven, and took the imperial throne. The state was named Great Tang, a general amnesty was proclaimed, and the era name was changed.

sentences.zh: 尊母晉國太夫人曹氏為皇太后，嫡母秦國夫人劉氏為皇太妃。

translations.literal: He honored his mother, Grand Lady Cao of the State of Jin, as Empress Dowager, and his father's principal wife, Lady Liu of the State of Qin, as Imperial Consort Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: He honored his mother, Grand Lady Cao of Jin, as Empress Dowager and his father's principal wife, Lady Liu of Qin, as Imperial Consort Dowager.

sentences.zh: 以豆盧革為門下侍郎，盧程為中書侍郎，並同平章事；

translations.literal: He appointed Doulu Ge Vice Minister of the Chancellery and Lu Cheng Vice Minister of the Secretariat, both concurrent Grand Councilors;
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Doulu Ge Vice Minister of the Chancellery and Lu Cheng Vice Minister of the Secretariat, both concurrent Grand Councilors;

sentences.zh: 郭崇韜、張居翰為樞密使，盧質、馮道為翰林學士，張憲為工部侍郎、租庸使，又以義武掌書記李德休為御史中丞。

translations.literal: Guo Chongtao and Zhang Juhan were made commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Lu Zhi and Feng Dao were made Hanlin academicians; Zhang Xian was made Vice Minister of Works and commissioner of land tax and corvée; and Li Dexiu, secretary of Yiwu, was made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao and Zhang Juhan became commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Lu Zhi and Feng Dao became Hanlin academicians; Zhang Xian became Vice Minister of Works and commissioner of land tax and corvée; and Li Dexiu, secretary of Yiwu, became Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 德林，絳之孫也。

translations.literal: Delin was a grandson of Li Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Delin was a grandson of Li Jiang.

sentences.zh: 詔盧程詣晉陽冊太后、太妃。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Lu Cheng to proceed to Jinyang to invest the Empress Dowager and the Imperial Consort Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Lu Cheng to proceed to Jinyang to invest the Empress Dowager and the Imperial Consort Dowager.

sentences.zh: 初，太妃無子，性賢，不妒忌；

translations.literal: Earlier, the Imperial Consort Dowager had borne no sons, was virtuous by nature, and was free of jealousy;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Imperial Consort Dowager had borne no sons. She was virtuous by nature and free of jealousy;

sentences.zh: 太后為武皇侍姬，太妃常勸武皇善待之，太后亦自謙退，由是相得甚歡。

translations.literal: the Empress Dowager had been a concubine of Emperor Wu, and the Imperial Consort Dowager often urged Emperor Wu to treat her well; the Empress Dowager also humbled herself, and thus the two were on very cordial terms.
translations.idiomatic: the Empress Dowager had been a concubine of Emperor Wu. The Imperial Consort Dowager often urged Emperor Wu to treat her well, and the Empress Dowager in turn humbled herself, so the two women were on very cordial terms.

sentences.zh: 及受冊，太妃詣太后宮賀，有喜色，太后忸怩不自安。

translations.literal: When the investiture took place, the Imperial Consort Dowager came to the Empress Dowager's palace to offer congratulations with a look of joy, while the Empress Dowager felt awkward and ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: At the investiture, the Imperial Consort Dowager came to the Empress Dowager's palace to congratulate her with evident joy, while the Empress Dowager felt awkward and ill at ease.

sentences.zh: 太妃曰：「願吾兒享國久長，吾輩獲沒於地，園陵有主，餘何足言！」

translations.literal: The Imperial Consort Dowager said, "May my son enjoy the realm for long years; may we both be laid in the earth, with the imperial tombs having their master—what more is there to say!"
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Consort Dowager said, "May my son reign long; may we both be laid in the earth with the imperial tombs secure—what more is there to say!"

sentences.zh: 因相向歔欷。

translations.literal: They then faced each other and wept.
translations.idiomatic: They then faced each other and wept.

sentences.zh: 豆盧革、盧程皆輕淺無它能，上以其衣冠之緒，霸府元僚，故用之。

translations.literal: Doulu Ge and Lu Cheng were both shallow men without other ability; the emperor employed them because they were scions of eminent families and veteran officials of the hegemonic headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Doulu Ge and Lu Cheng were both shallow men without other real ability. The emperor employed them because they were scions of eminent families and veteran officials of his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 初，李紹宏為中門使，郭崇韜副之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Shaohong had been director of the Central Gate and Guo Chongtao his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Shaohong had served as director of the Central Gate with Guo Chongtao as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 至是，自幽州召還，崇韜惡其舊人位在己上，乃薦張居翰為樞密使，以紹宏為宣徽使，紹宏由是恨之。

translations.literal: At this time he was recalled from You Prefecture; Chongtao resented that this old associate outranked him, and therefore recommended Zhang Juhan as commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs while assigning Shaohong to be commissioner of the Palace Secretariat—Shaohong therefore bore a grudge against him.
translations.idiomatic: Now he was recalled from You Prefecture. Chongtao resented that this old associate outranked him, so he recommended Zhang Juhan as commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and assigned Shaohong to the Palace Secretariat instead—Shaohong therefore came to hate him.

sentences.zh: 居翰和謹畏事，軍國機政皆崇韜掌之。

translations.literal: Juhan was mild, cautious, and deferential in office; all military and state affairs were managed by Chongtao.
translations.idiomatic: Juhan was mild, cautious, and deferential in office, and Chongtao managed all military and state affairs.

sentences.zh: 支度務使孔謙自謂才能勤效，應為租庸使；

translations.literal: Kong Qian, commissioner of revenue and expenditure, considered himself talented and diligent and fit to be commissioner of land tax and corvée;
translations.idiomatic: Kong Qian, commissioner of revenue and expenditure, believed himself talented and diligent and fit to be commissioner of land tax and corvée;

sentences.zh: 眾議以謙人微地寒，不當遽總重任，故崇韜薦張憲，以謙副之，謙亦不悅。

translations.literal: general opinion held that Qian was of humble birth and low station and should not suddenly be given overall responsibility, so Chongtao recommended Zhang Xian and made Qian his deputy—Qian too was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: opinion held that Qian was of humble birth and should not suddenly be given overall responsibility, so Chongtao recommended Zhang Xian and made Qian his deputy—Qian too was displeased.

sentences.zh: 以魏州為興唐府，建東京。

translations.literal: Weizhou was made the Xingtang metropolitan prefecture and established as the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhou was made the Xingtang metropolitan prefecture and established as the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 又於太原府建西京，又以鎮州為真定府，建北都。

translations.literal: The Taiyuan metropolitan prefecture was also established as the Western Capital, and Zhen Prefecture was made the Zhending metropolitan prefecture and established as the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan was also established as the Western Capital, and Zhen Prefecture was made the Zhending metropolitan prefecture and established as the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 以魏博節度判官王正言為禮部尚書，行興唐尹；

translations.literal: Wang Zhengyan, judge of the Weibo military commission, was made Minister of Rites and acting prefect of Xingtang;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhengyan, judge of the Weibo commission, was made Minister of Rites and acting prefect of Xingtang;

sentences.zh: 太原馬步都虞候孟知祥為太原尹，充西京副留守；

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang, overall commander of horse and foot at Taiyuan, was made prefect of Taiyuan and deputy defender of the Western Capital;
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang, overall commander of horse and foot at Taiyuan, was made prefect of Taiyuan and deputy defender of the Western Capital;

sentences.zh: 潞州觀察判官任圜為工部尚書，兼真定尹，充北京副留守；

translations.literal: Ren Yuan, judge of the Lu observation commission, was made Vice Minister of Works and concurrent prefect of Zhending, serving as deputy defender of the Northern Capital;
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yuan, judge of the Lu observation commission, was made Vice Minister of Works and concurrent prefect of Zhending, serving as deputy defender of the Northern Capital;

sentences.zh: 皇子繼岌為北都留守、興聖宮使，判不軍諸衛事。

translations.literal: the imperial son Jiji was made defender of the Northern Capital and commissioner of the Xingsheng Palace, with charge over the various guards of the forbidden army.
translations.idiomatic: the imperial son Jiji was made defender of the Northern Capital and commissioner of the Xingsheng Palace, with charge over the various guards of the forbidden army.

sentences.zh: 時唐國所有凡十三節度、五十州。

translations.literal: At this time the Tang state possessed thirteen military commissions and fifty prefectures in all.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the Tang state possessed thirteen military commissions and fifty prefectures in all.

sentences.zh: 閏月，追尊皇曾祖執宜曰懿祖昭烈皇帝，祖國昌曰獻祖文皇帝，考晉王曰太祖武皇帝。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, the emperor's great-grandfather Zhike was posthumously honored as Emperor Zhaolie, the Founding Exalted Ancestor; his grandfather Guochang as Emperor Wen, the Founding Offering Ancestor; and his father the Prince of Jin as Emperor Wu, the Founding Martial Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, the emperor posthumously honored his great-grandfather Zhike as Emperor Zhaolie, the Founding Exalted Ancestor; his grandfather Guochang as Emperor Wen, the Founding Offering Ancestor; and his father the Prince of Jin as Emperor Wu, the Founding Martial Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 立宗廟於晉陽，以高祖、太宗、懿宗、昭宗洎懿祖以下為七室。

translations.literal: An ancestral temple was established at Jinyang, with seven shrines for Gaozu, Taizong, Yizong, Zhaozong, and the line from the Exalted Ancestor downward.
translations.idiomatic: An ancestral temple was established at Jinyang with seven shrines for Gaozu, Taizong, Yizong, Zhaozong, and the line from the Exalted Ancestor downward.

sentences.zh: 甲午，契丹寇幽州，至易定而還。

translations.literal: On jiawu the Khitan raided You Prefecture, reaching Yi and Ding and then returning.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu the Khitan raided You Prefecture, reached Yi and Ding, and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時契丹屢入寇，鈔掠饋運，幽州食不支半年，衛州為梁所取，潞州內叛，人情岌岌，以為梁未可取，帝患之。

translations.literal: At this time the Khitan repeatedly invaded, plundering supply convoys; You Prefecture could not sustain itself on stored grain for half a year; Wei Prefecture had been taken by Liang; Lu Prefecture had rebelled within; popular sentiment was precarious; and it was thought that Liang could not yet be taken—the emperor was troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan were raiding repeatedly and plundering supply convoys. You Prefecture could not sustain itself on stored grain for half a year; Wei Prefecture had fallen to Liang; Lu Prefecture had rebelled within; morale was precarious; and many believed Liang could not yet be defeated—the emperor was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 會鄆州將盧順密來奔。

translations.literal: Just then Lu Shunmi, an officer of Yan Prefecture, came over in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Lu Shunmi, an officer of Yan Prefecture, defected to Tang.

sentences.zh: 先是，梁天平節度使戴思遠屯楊村，留順密與巡檢使劉遂嚴、都指揮使燕顒守鄆州。

translations.literal: Earlier, Dai Siyuan, military commissioner of Tianping under Liang, had encamped at Yang Village and left Shunmi, together with inspection commissioner Liu Suoyan and overall commander Yan Yong, to defend Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Dai Siyuan, Liang military commissioner of Tianping, had encamped at Yang Village and left Shunmi, together with inspection commissioner Liu Suoyan and overall commander Yan Yong, to defend Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 順密言於帝曰：「鄆州守兵不滿千人，遂嚴、顒皆失眾心，可襲取也。」

translations.literal: Shunmi said to the emperor, "The garrison of Yan Prefecture numbers fewer than a thousand men; Suoyan and Yong have both lost the hearts of the troops—it can be seized by surprise."
translations.idiomatic: Shunmi told the emperor, "Yan Prefecture has fewer than a thousand defenders, and Suoyan and Yong have both lost the troops' loyalty—it can be taken by surprise."

sentences.zh: 郭崇韜等皆以為「懸軍遠襲，萬一不利，虛棄數千人，順密不可從。」

translations.literal: Guo Chongtao and the others all said, "To send an isolated force on a distant surprise attack—if by any chance it goes badly, several thousand men will be wasted in vain; Shunmi must not be followed."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao and the others all objected: "A distant surprise raid with a detached force risks wasting several thousand men if anything goes wrong—Shunmi's plan should not be followed."

sentences.zh: 帝密召李嗣源於帳中謀之曰：「梁人志在吞澤潞，不備東方，若得東平，則潰其心腹。

translations.literal: The emperor secretly summoned Li Siyuan into his tent to consult him, saying, "The Liang aim to swallow Ze and Lu and are unprepared in the east; if we take Dongping, we will rupture their heartland.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly summoned Li Siyuan into his tent and said, "The Liang are bent on swallowing Ze and Lu and are unprepared in the east. If we take Dongping, we will strike at their heartland.

sentences.zh: 東平果可取乎？」

translations.literal: Can Dongping truly be taken?"
translations.idiomatic: Can Dongping truly be taken?"

sentences.zh: 嗣源自胡柳有渡河之慚，常欲立奇功以補過，對曰：「今用兵歲久，生民疲弊，苟非出奇取勝，大功何由可成！

translations.literal: Siyuan, since Huliang bore the shame of the river crossing, had long wished to win a singular exploit to redeem himself, and replied, "War has now dragged on for years and the people are worn out; unless we win by an unexpected stroke, how can a great achievement be accomplished!
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan still bore the shame of the river crossing at Huliang and longed to redeem himself with a singular exploit. He replied, "The war has dragged on for years and the people are exhausted. Unless we win by an unexpected stroke, how can we achieve a great victory!

sentences.zh: 臣願獨當此役，必有以報。」

translations.literal: Your subject is willing to undertake this campaign alone and will surely have something to report in return."
translations.idiomatic: I am willing to undertake this campaign alone and will surely bring you news of success."

sentences.zh: 帝悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，遣嗣源將所部精兵五千自德勝趣鄆州。

translations.literal: On renyin he dispatched Siyuan to lead five thousand picked troops of his command from Desheng toward Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin he dispatched Siyuan with five thousand picked troops from Desheng toward Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 比及楊劉，日已暮，陰雨道黑，將士皆不欲進，高行周曰：「此天讚我也，彼必無備。」

translations.literal: By the time they reached Yangliu, the day was already ending; rain fell and the road was dark; officers and soldiers alike were unwilling to advance. Gao Xingzhou said, "Heaven is aiding us—the enemy will surely be unprepared."
translations.idiomatic: By the time they reached Yangliu, night was falling, rain had darkened the road, and the troops were reluctant to advance. Gao Xingzhou said, "Heaven is aiding us—the enemy will surely be unprepared."

sentences.zh: 夜，渡河至城下，鄆人不知，李從珂先登，殺守卒，啟關納外兵，進攻牙城，城中大擾。

translations.literal: At night they crossed the river to the foot of the wall; the people of Yan did not know. Li Congke was first to ascend, killed the gate guards, opened the pass and admitted the outside troops, and advanced to attack the headquarters compound; great disorder arose within the city.
translations.idiomatic: That night they crossed the river to the foot of the wall before the people of Yan knew what was happening. Li Congke was first over the wall, killed the gate guards, opened the pass to admit the outside troops, and advanced on the headquarters compound as the city fell into uproar.

sentences.zh: 癸卯旦，嗣源兵盡入，遂拔牙城，劉遂嚴、燕顒奔大梁。

translations.literal: At dawn on guimao, Siyuan's troops had all entered; they then stormed the headquarters compound, and Liu Suoyan and Yan Yong fled to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on guimao, Siyuan's troops had all entered, stormed the headquarters compound, and Liu Suoyan and Yan Yong fled to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 嗣源禁焚掠，撫吏民，執知州事節度副使崔簹、判官趙鳳送興唐。

translations.literal: Siyuan forbade burning and plunder, reassured officials and people, seized Cui Qian, deputy commissioner acting as prefect, and judge Zhao Feng, and sent them to Xingtang.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan forbade burning and plunder, reassured officials and civilians, seized acting prefect Cui Qian and judge Zhao Feng, and sent them to Xingtang.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜曰：「總管真奇才，吾事集矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said in great joy, "The overall commander is truly a rare talent—my enterprise is assured."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said in delight, "The overall commander is truly a rare talent—my enterprise is assured."

sentences.zh: 即以嗣源為天平節度使。

translations.literal: He thereupon appointed Siyuan military commissioner of Tianping.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon appointed Siyuan military commissioner of Tianping.

sentences.zh: 梁主聞鄆州失守，大懼，斬劉遂嚴、燕顒於市，罷戴思遠招討使，降授宣化留後，遣使詰讓北面諸將段凝、王彥章等，趣令進戰。

translations.literal: When the Liang emperor heard that Yan Prefecture had fallen, he was greatly afraid; he executed Liu Suoyan and Yan Yong in the marketplace, removed Dai Siyuan as frontier campaign commissioner and demoted him to acting commissioner of Xuanhua, and sent envoys to rebuke the northern generals Duan Ning, Wang Yanzhang, and others, urging them to advance and give battle.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang emperor learned that Yan Prefecture had fallen, he was terrified. He executed Liu Suoyan and Yan Yong in the marketplace, removed Dai Siyuan as frontier campaign commissioner and demoted him to acting commissioner of Xuanhua, and sent envoys to rebuke the northern generals Duan Ning, Wang Yanzhang, and others, ordering them to advance and fight.

sentences.zh: 敬翔知梁室已危，以繩內靴中，入見梁主曰：「先帝取天下，不以臣為不肖，所謀無不用。

translations.literal: Jing Xiang knew the Liang house was already in peril; he hid a cord inside his boot, entered to see the Liang emperor, and said, "The late emperor took the realm and did not consider your subject unworthy—none of his plans went unused.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Xiang knew the Liang house was already in peril. He hid a cord in his boot, went in to see the Liang emperor, and said, "The late emperor took the realm and did not consider me unworthy—none of his plans went unused.

sentences.zh: 今敵勢益強，而陛下棄忽臣言。

translations.literal: Now the enemy grows ever stronger, yet Your Majesty disregards your subject's words.
translations.idiomatic: Now the enemy grows ever stronger, yet Your Majesty disregards my counsel.

sentences.zh: 臣身無用，不如死！」

translations.literal: Your subject's person is useless—better to die!"
translations.idiomatic: I am useless—better to die!"

sentences.zh: 引繩將自經。

translations.literal: He drew out the cord and was about to hang himself.
translations.idiomatic: He drew out the cord and was about to hang himself.

sentences.zh: 梁主止之，問所欲言，翔曰：「事急矣，非用王彥章為大將，不可救也。」

translations.literal: The Liang emperor stopped him and asked what he wished to say; Xiang said, "The situation is urgent—unless Wang Yanzhang is made grand general, it cannot be saved."
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor stopped him and asked what he wished to say. Xiang said, "The situation is urgent—unless Wang Yanzhang is made grand general, nothing can save us."

sentences.zh: 梁主從之，以彥章代思遠為北面招討使，仍以段凝為副。

translations.literal: The Liang emperor followed this advice, making Yanzhang frontier campaign commissioner of the north in Siyuan's place, with Ning still as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor agreed, making Yanzhang frontier campaign commissioner of the north in place of Siyuan, with Ning still as deputy.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，自將親軍屯澶州，命蕃漢馬步都虞候朱守殷守德勝，戒之曰：「王鐵槍勇決，乘憤激之氣，必來唐突，宜謹備之。」

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of this, he personally led the imperial guard to encamp at Cang Prefecture and ordered Zhu Shouyin, overall commander of Khitan and Han horse and foot, to defend Desheng, admonishing him: "Wang the Iron Spear is fierce and resolute; riding the force of anger and urgency, he is sure to come in a sudden rush—you must prepare carefully."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this, he personally led the imperial guard to encamp at Cang Prefecture and ordered Zhu Shouyin, overall commander of Khitan and Han horse and foot, to defend Desheng, warning him: "Wang the Iron Spear is fierce and resolute. Riding a wave of anger, he is sure to strike suddenly—you must prepare carefully."

sentences.zh: 守殷，王幼時所役蒼頭也。

translations.literal: Shouyin had been a household servant in the emperor's youth.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyin had been a household servant in the emperor's youth.

sentences.zh: 又遣使遺吳王書，告以已克鄆州，請同舉兵擊梁。

translations.literal: He also sent envoys with a letter to the King of Wu, informing him that Yan Prefecture had been taken and asking that they jointly raise troops to strike Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent envoys with a letter to the King of Wu, reporting the capture of Yan Prefecture and asking that they jointly raise troops against Liang.

sentences.zh: 五月，使者至吳，徐溫欲持兩端，將舟師循海而北，助其勝者。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the envoys reached Wu; Xu Wen wished to keep both sides in play and was about to lead a fleet north along the sea to aid whichever side prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the envoys reached Wu. Xu Wen wished to keep both sides in play and planned to lead a fleet north along the coast to aid whichever side prevailed.

sentences.zh: 嚴可求曰：「若梁人邀我登陸為援，何以拒之？」

translations.literal: Yan Keqiu said, "If the Liang invite us ashore as reinforcements, how shall we refuse?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan Keqiu said, "If the Liang invite us ashore as reinforcements, how can we refuse?"

sentences.zh: 溫乃止。

translations.literal: Wen thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Wen thereupon abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 梁主召問王彥章以破敵之期，彥章對曰：「三日。」

translations.literal: The Liang emperor summoned Wang Yanzhang and asked him the time needed to defeat the enemy; Yanzhang replied, "Three days."
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor summoned Wang Yanzhang and asked how long he needed to defeat the enemy. Yanzhang replied, "Three days."

sentences.zh: 左右皆失笑。

translations.literal: Those at his side all laughed aloud.
translations.idiomatic: Those around him all laughed aloud.

sentences.zh: 彥章出，兩日，馳至滑州。

translations.literal: Yanzhang went out; within two days he galloped to Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhang departed, and within two days he galloped to Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，置酒大會，陰遣人具舟於楊村；

translations.literal: On xinyou he held a great banquet and secretly sent men to prepare boats at Yang Village;
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou he held a great banquet and secretly sent men to prepare boats at Yang Village;

sentences.zh: 夜，命甲士六百，皆持巨斧，載冶者，具□炭，乘流而下。

translations.literal: at night he ordered six hundred armored soldiers, all bearing great axes, with smiths aboard and charcoal prepared, to float downstream.
translations.idiomatic: that night he ordered six hundred armored soldiers, all bearing great axes, with smiths aboard and charcoal at hand, to float downstream.

sentences.zh: 會飲尚未散，彥章陽起更衣，引精兵數千循河南岸趨德勝。

translations.literal: Just as the drinking had not yet ended, Yanzhang pretended to rise to change clothes and led several thousand picked troops along the south bank of the river toward Desheng.
translations.idiomatic: While the banquet was still in progress, Yanzhang pretended to leave to change clothes and led several thousand picked troops along the south bank of the river toward Desheng.

sentences.zh: 天微雨，朱安殷不為備，舟中兵舉鎖燒斷之，因以巨斧斬浮橋，而彥章引兵急擊南城。

translations.literal: A light rain fell; Zhu Shouyin made no preparations; the soldiers in the boats raised burning torches to sever the chains, then used great axes to chop through the pontoon bridge, while Yanzhang led troops in a swift assault on the southern city.
translations.idiomatic: A light rain was falling and Zhu Shouyin was unprepared. The soldiers in the boats used torches to burn through the chains, then chopped the pontoon bridge with great axes while Yanzhang led a swift assault on the southern city.

sentences.zh: 浮橋斷，南城遂破，斬首數千級。

translations.literal: The pontoon bridge was severed and the southern city was then taken; several thousand heads were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The pontoon bridge was severed, the southern city fell, and several thousand heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 時受命適三日矣。

translations.literal: It was now exactly three days since he had received his commission.
translations.idiomatic: It was now exactly three days since he had received his commission.

sentences.zh: 守殷以小舟載甲士濟河救之，不及。

translations.literal: Shouyin ferried armored soldiers across the river in small boats to rescue the city, but could not arrive in time.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyin ferried armored soldiers across the river in small boats to rescue the city but could not arrive in time.

sentences.zh: 彥章進攻潘張、麻家口、景店諸寨，皆拔之，聲勢大振。

translations.literal: Yanzhang advanced to attack the stockades at Panzhang, Majiakou, Jingdian, and elsewhere, capturing them all; his momentum swelled greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhang advanced against the stockades at Panzhang, Majiakou, Jingdian, and elsewhere, capturing them all, and his momentum swelled greatly.

sentences.zh: 帝遣宦者焦彥賓急趣楊劉，與鎮使李周固守，命守殷棄德勝北城，撤屋為筏，載兵械浮河東下，助楊劉守備，徙其芻糧薪炭於澶州，所耗失殆半。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the eunuch Jiao Yanbin in haste to Yangliu to hold firm with garrison commissioner Li Zhou; he ordered Shouyin to abandon the northern city of Desheng, tear down houses to make rafts, load weapons and float down the eastern river to reinforce Yangliu's defenses, and move its fodder, grain, fuel, and charcoal to Cang Prefecture—nearly half was lost in the process.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the eunuch Jiao Yanbin in haste to Yangliu to hold firm with garrison commissioner Li Zhou. He ordered Shouyin to abandon the northern city of Desheng, tear down houses to make rafts, load weapons, and float downriver to reinforce Yangliu, moving its fodder, grain, fuel, and charcoal to Cang Prefecture—nearly half was lost in the process.

sentences.zh: 王彥章亦撤南城屋材浮河而下，各行一岸，每遇灣曲，輒於中流交鬥，飛矢雨集，或全舟覆沒，一日百戰，互有勝負。

translations.literal: Wang Yanzhang likewise tore down houses in the southern city and floated the timber downriver; each side kept to one bank, and whenever they met a bend they would fight in midstream—arrows fell like rain, boats were sometimes entirely sunk, a hundred battles in a day, victory and defeat alternating.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanzhang likewise tore down houses in the southern city and floated the timber downriver. Each side kept to one bank, and whenever they met a bend they fought in midstream—arrows fell like rain, boats were sometimes sunk outright, and a hundred battles might be fought in a day with victory alternating between them.

sentences.zh: 比及楊劉，殆亡士卒之半。

translations.literal: By the time they reached Yangliu, nearly half the soldiers had perished.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they reached Yangliu, nearly half their soldiers had been lost.

sentences.zh: 己巳，王彥章、段凝以十萬之眾攻楊劉，百道俱進，晝夜不息，連巨艦九艘，橫亙河津以絕援兵。

translations.literal: On jisi, Wang Yanzhang and Duan Ning attacked Yangliu with a force of a hundred thousand, advancing on a hundred routes without cease day or night; they linked nine great warships across the river crossing to cut off relief troops.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Wang Yanzhang and Duan Ning attacked Yangliu with a hundred thousand men, advancing on a hundred routes without cease day or night. They linked nine great warships across the river crossing to cut off relief troops.

sentences.zh: 城垂陷者數四，賴李周悉力拒之，與士卒同甘苦，彥章不能克，退屯城南，為連營以守之。

translations.literal: The city was on the verge of falling four times; thanks to Li Zhou's all-out resistance, sharing hardship with the soldiers, Yanzhang could not take it; he withdrew to encamp south of the city and built a chain of camps to besiege it.
translations.idiomatic: The city was on the verge of falling four times, but Li Zhou resisted with all his strength, sharing hardship with his soldiers, and Yanzhang could not take it. He withdrew to encamp south of the city and built a chain of camps to besiege it.

sentences.zh: 楊劉告急於帝，請日行百里以赴之；

translations.literal: Yangliu sent urgent word to the emperor, asking that he march a hundred li a day to come to its aid;
translations.idiomatic: Yangliu sent urgent word to the emperor, asking that he march a hundred li a day to its relief;

sentences.zh: 帝引兵救之，曰：「李周在內，何憂！」

translations.literal: the emperor led troops to rescue it, saying, "With Li Zhou inside, what is there to worry about!"
translations.idiomatic: the emperor led troops to the rescue, saying, "With Li Zhou inside, what is there to worry about!"

sentences.zh: 日行六十里，不廢畋獵，六月，乙亥，至楊劉。

translations.literal: He marched sixty li a day without giving up hunting; in the sixth month, on yihai, he reached Yangliu.
translations.idiomatic: He marched sixty li a day without giving up hunting. In the sixth month, on yihai, he reached Yangliu.

sentences.zh: 梁兵塹壘重複，嚴不可入，帝患之，問計於郭崇韜，對曰：「今彥章據守津要，意謂可以坐取東平；

translations.literal: The Liang army's trenches and ramparts were layered in depth, sternly impregnable; the emperor was troubled by this and asked Guo Chongtao for a plan. Chongtao replied, "Now Yanzhang holds the river crossings and strong points, intending to take Dongping without effort;
translations.idiomatic: The Liang army's trenches and ramparts were layered in depth and could not be breached; the emperor was troubled and asked Guo Chongtao for a plan. Chongtao replied, "Yanzhang now holds the river crossings and strong points, expecting to take Dongping without a fight;

sentences.zh: 苟大軍不南，則東平不守矣。

translations.literal: if the great army does not march south, Dongping cannot be held.
translations.idiomatic: if the main army does not march south, Dongping cannot be held.

sentences.zh: 臣請築壘於博州東岸以固河津，既得以應接東平，又可以分賊兵勢。

translations.literal: Your subject asks to build ramparts on the east bank of Bo Prefecture to secure the river crossing—thus we can both support Dongping and divide the enemy's strength.
translations.idiomatic: I ask to build ramparts on the east bank of Bo Prefecture to secure the river crossing. That way we can support Dongping and divide the enemy's strength at the same time.

sentences.zh: 但慮彥章詗知，逕來薄我，城不能就，願陛下募敢死之士，日令挑戰以綴之，苟彥章旬日不東，則城成矣。」

translations.literal: But I fear Yanzhang will learn of it and come straight to press us, and the city will not be finished. I ask Your Majesty to enlist dare-to-die men and order daily challenges to hold him back—if Yanzhang does not go east for ten days, the city will be complete."
translations.idiomatic: But I fear Yanzhang will learn of it and come straight to attack us before the city is finished. I ask Your Majesty to enlist dare-to-die men and send out daily challenges to hold him back. If Yanzhang does not move east for ten days, the city will be complete."

sentences.zh: 時李嗣源守鄆州，河北聲問不通，人心漸離，不保朝夕。

translations.literal: At this time Li Siyuan was defending Yan Prefecture; north of the Yellow River no word could get through; hearts were gradually turning away; no one could count on surviving from one day to the next.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Li Siyuan was defending Yan Prefecture. North of the Yellow River no word could get through, morale was slipping, and no one could count on living from one day to the next.

sentences.zh: 會梁右先鋒指揮使康延孝密請降於嗣源，延孝者，太原胡人，有罪，亡奔梁，時隸段凝麾下。

translations.literal: Just then Kang Yanxiao, the Liang Right Vanguard Commanding Officer, secretly asked to surrender to Siyuan. Yanxiao was a Hu man from Taiyuan who, having committed a crime, fled to Liang and was then under Duan Ning's command.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Kang Yanxiao, the Liang Right Vanguard Commanding Officer, secretly asked to surrender to Siyuan. Yanxiao was a Hu man from Taiyuan who had fled to Liang after committing a crime and was then serving under Duan Ning.

sentences.zh: 嗣源遣押牙臨漳范延光送延孝蠟書詣帝，延光因言於帝曰：「楊劉控扼已固，梁人必不能取，請築壘馬家口以通鄆州之路。」

translations.literal: Siyuan sent his adjutant Fan Yanguang of Linzhang to deliver Yanxiao's sealed letter to the emperor; Yanguang thereupon said to the emperor, "The Yangliu crossing is already firmly held—Liang troops cannot take it. I ask to build ramparts at Majiakou to open a route to Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan sent his adjutant Fan Yanguang of Linzhang to deliver Yanxiao's sealed letter to the emperor. Yanguang then told the emperor, "The Yangliu crossing is already firmly held and Liang troops cannot take it. I ask to build ramparts at Majiakou to open a route to Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 帝從之，遣崇韜將萬人夜發，倍道趣博州，至馬家口渡河，築城晝夜不息。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this advice, sent Chongtao with ten thousand men to set out at night, took double marches toward Bo Prefecture, crossed the river at Majiakou, and built the city without cease day and night.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and sent Chongtao with ten thousand men to set out at night. They took forced marches toward Bo Prefecture, crossed the river at Majiakou, and built the city without cease day and night.

sentences.zh: 帝在楊劉，與梁人晝夜苦戰。

translations.literal: The emperor was at Yangliu, fighting bitterly with Liang troops day and night.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remained at Yangliu, fighting bitterly with Liang troops day and night.

sentences.zh: 崇韜築新城凡六日，王彥章聞之，將兵數萬人馳至，戊子，急攻新城，連巨艦十餘艘於中流以絕援路。

translations.literal: Chongtao built the new city in all of six days; Wang Yanzhang heard of it and led tens of thousands of troops at full speed to the spot; on wuzi he pressed the attack on the new city and moored more than ten great warships in midstream to cut off the route of relief.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao finished the new city in six days. When Wang Yanzhang heard of it, he led tens of thousands of troops at full speed to the spot. On wuzi he pressed the attack on the new city and moored more than ten great warships in midstream to cut off the route of relief.

sentences.zh: 時板築僅畢，城猶卑下，沙土疏惡，未有樓魯及守備；

translations.literal: At that time the walls had only just been finished; the city was still low; the sand and earth were loose and poor; there were neither towers nor defenses yet;
translations.idiomatic: The walls had only just been finished. The city was still low, the sand and earth loose and poor, and there were neither towers nor proper defenses yet;

sentences.zh: 崇韜慰勞士卒，以身先之，四面拒戰，遣間使告急於帝。

translations.literal: Chongtao comforted the soldiers, led from the front himself, resisted on all four sides, and sent secret messengers to report the emergency to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao comforted the soldiers, led from the front himself, fought on all four sides, and sent secret messengers to report the emergency to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝自楊劉引大軍救之，陳於新城西岸，城中望之增氣，大呼叱梁軍，梁人斷紲斂艦；

translations.literal: The emperor led a great army from Yangliu to the rescue and deployed west of the new city on the riverbank; the men in the city saw this and their spirits rose; they shouted abuse at the Liang army; the Liang men cut their cables and gathered in their ships;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor led a great army from Yangliu to the rescue and deployed on the west bank opposite the new city. The men in the city saw this and their spirits rose; they shouted abuse at the Liang army, and the Liang men cut their cables and gathered in their ships;

sentences.zh: 帝艤舟將渡，彥章解圍，退保鄒家口。

translations.literal: The emperor moored his boats and was about to cross when Yanzhang lifted the siege and withdrew to hold Zoujiakou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor moored his boats and was about to cross when Yanzhang lifted the siege and withdrew to hold Zoujiakou.

sentences.zh: 鄆州奏報始通。

translations.literal: Reports from Yan Prefecture began to get through.
translations.idiomatic: Reports from Yan Prefecture began to get through at last.

sentences.zh: 李嗣源密表請正朱守殷覆軍之罪，帝不從。

translations.literal: Li Siyuan secretly memorialized asking that Zhu Shouyin be punished for destroying his army; the emperor would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siyuan secretly memorialized asking that Zhu Shouyin be punished for losing his army, but the emperor would not agree.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丁未，帝引兵循河而南，彥章等棄鄒家口，復趣楊劉。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on dingwei, the emperor led troops south along the river; Yanzhang and the others abandoned Zoujiakou and hurried back toward Yangliu.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on dingwei, the emperor led troops south along the river. Yanzhang and the others abandoned Zoujiakou and hurried back toward Yangliu.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，游弈將李紹興敗梁遊兵於清丘驛南。

translations.literal: On jiayin, roving campaign general Li Shaoxing defeated Liang scouting troops south of Qingqiu Post.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, roving campaign general Li Shaoxing defeated Liang scouting troops south of Qingqiu Post.

sentences.zh: 段凝以為唐兵已自上流渡，驚駭失色，面數彥章，尤其深入。

translations.literal: Duan Ning thought Tang troops had already crossed from upriver; he turned pale with alarm and face-to-face rebuked Yanzhang, blaming him especially for advancing so far.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ning thought Tang troops had already crossed from upriver. He turned pale with alarm and rebuked Yanzhang to his face, blaming him especially for advancing so deep.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，蜀侍中魏王宗侃卒。

translations.literal: On yimao, Shu Grand Councillor Prince Wei Zongkan died.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Shu Grand Councillor Prince Wei Zongkan died.

sentences.zh: 戊午，帝遣騎將李紹榮直抵梁營，擒其斥候，梁人益恐，又以火筏焚其連艦。

translations.literal: On wuwu, the emperor sent cavalry commander Li Shaorong straight to the Liang camp and captured their scouts; Liang troops grew ever more fearful and again set fire-rafts to burn their linked warships.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, the emperor sent cavalry commander Li Shaorong straight to the Liang camp and captured their scouts. Liang troops grew ever more fearful and again set fire-rafts to burn their linked warships.

sentences.zh: 王彥章等聞帝引兵已至鄒家口，己未，解楊劉圍，走保楊村；

translations.literal: Wang Yanzhang and the others heard the emperor had already led troops to Zoujiakou; on jiwei they lifted the siege of Yangliu and fled to hold Yang Village;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanzhang and the others heard the emperor had already led troops to Zoujiakou. On jiwei they lifted the siege of Yangliu and fled to hold Yang Village;

sentences.zh: 唐兵追擊之，復屯德勝。

translations.literal: Tang troops pursued and re-encamped at Desheng.
translations.idiomatic: Tang troops pursued them and re-encamped at Desheng.

sentences.zh: 梁兵前後急攻諸城，士卒遭矢石、溺水、□曷死者且萬人，委棄資糧、鎧仗、鍋幕，動以千計。

translations.literal: Before and after, the Liang army had pressed attacks on several cities; soldiers killed by arrows and stones, drowning, and heatstroke numbered nearly ten thousand; abandoned supplies, grain, armor, weapons, and camp gear ran to thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Before and after, the Liang army had pressed attacks on several cities. Nearly ten thousand soldiers were killed by arrows and stones, drowning, and heatstroke, and abandoned supplies, grain, armor, weapons, and camp gear ran to the thousands.

sentences.zh: 楊劉比至圍解，城中無食已三日矣。

translations.literal: By the time Yangliu's siege was lifted, the city had been without food for three days.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Yangliu's siege was lifted, the city had been without food for three days.

sentences.zh: 王彥章疾趙、張亂政，及為招討使，謂所親曰：「待我成功還，當盡誅奸臣以謝天下！」

translations.literal: Wang Yanzhang hated Zhao and Zhang's corrupt governance, and when he became campaign commissioner he told those close to him, "Wait until I return successful—I shall execute every villainous minister to answer to the realm!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanzhang hated Zhao and Zhang's corrupt governance. When he became campaign commissioner he told those close to him, "Wait until I return successful—I shall execute every villainous minister to answer to the realm!

sentences.zh: 趙、張聞之，私相謂曰：「我輩寧死於沙陀，不可為彥章所殺。」

translations.literal: Zhao and Zhang heard this and said to each other in private, "We would rather die at the hands of the Shatuo than be killed by Yanzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao and Zhang heard this and said to each other in private, "We would rather die at the hands of the Shatuo than be killed by Yanzhang.

sentences.zh: 相與協力傾之。

translations.literal: Together they joined forces to bring him down.
translations.idiomatic: Together they joined forces to bring him down.

sentences.zh: 段凝素疾彥章之能而諂附趙、張，在軍中與彥章動相違戾，百方沮撓之，惟恐其有功，潛伺彥章過失以聞於梁主。

translations.literal: Duan Ning had always resented Yanzhang's ability while fawning on Zhao and Zhang; in the army he constantly clashed with Yanzhang and blocked him in every way, fearing only that he might win merit, and secretly watched for Yanzhang's faults to report to the Liang emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ning had always resented Yanzhang's ability while fawning on Zhao and Zhang. In the army he constantly clashed with Yanzhang and obstructed him in every way, fearing only that he might win merit, and secretly watched for Yanzhang's faults to report to the Liang emperor.

sentences.zh: 每捷奏至，趙、張悉歸功於凝，由是彥章功竟無成。

translations.literal: Whenever victory reports arrived, Zhao and Zhang attributed all credit to Ning, so Yanzhang's achievements came to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever victory reports arrived, Zhao and Zhang attributed all credit to Ning, so Yanzhang's achievements came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 及歸楊村，梁主信讒，猶恐彥章旦夕成功難制，征還大梁。

translations.literal: When they returned to Yang Village the Liang emperor believed slander and, still fearing Yanzhang might succeed at any moment and become hard to control, summoned him back to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When they returned to Yang Village the Liang emperor believed slander and, still fearing Yanzhang might succeed at any moment and become hard to control, summoned him back to Liang.

sentences.zh: 使將兵會董璋攻澤州。

translations.literal: He ordered him to lead troops to join Dong Zhang in attacking Ze Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered him to lead troops to join Dong Zhang in attacking Ze Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 甲子，帝至楊劉勞李周曰：「微卿善守，吾事敗矣。」

translations.literal: On jiazi the emperor reached Yangliu and thanked Li Zhou, saying, "But for your able defense, my cause would have failed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the emperor reached Yangliu and thanked Li Zhou, saying, "But for your able defense, my cause would have failed.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎、同平章事盧程以私事幹興唐府，府吏不能應，鞭吏背。

translations.literal: Vice Grand Councillor Lu Cheng came to Xingtang Prefecture on private business; the prefectural clerks could not accommodate him, so he flogged one on the back.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Grand Councillor Lu Cheng came to Xingtang Prefecture on private business. The prefectural clerks could not accommodate him, so he flogged one on the back.

sentences.zh: 光祿卿兼興唐少尹任團，圜之弟，帝之從姊婿也，詣程訴之。

translations.literal: Director of Imperial Entertainments and concurrent Xingtang Assistant Governor Ren Tuan—Yuan's younger brother and the emperor's cousin's husband—went to Cheng to complain.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Imperial Entertainments and concurrent Xingtang Assistant Governor Ren Tuan—Yuan's younger brother and the emperor's cousin's husband—went to Cheng to complain.

sentences.zh: 程罵曰：「公何等蟲豸，欲倚婦力邪！」

translations.literal: Cheng cursed him, "What sort of insect are you, trying to rely on a wife's family power!
translations.idiomatic: Cheng cursed him, "What sort of insect are you, trying to rely on your wife's family for power!

sentences.zh: 團訴於帝。

translations.literal: Tuan complained to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Tuan complained to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「朕誤相此癡物，乃敢辱吾九卿！」

translations.literal: The emperor said in anger, "I mistakenly made this fool chancellor—he dares insult one of my Nine Ministers!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said in anger, "I mistakenly made this fool chancellor—he dares insult one of my Nine Ministers!

sentences.zh: 欲賜自盡；

translations.literal: He wanted to grant him suicide;
translations.idiomatic: He wanted to grant him suicide;

sentences.zh: 盧質力救之，乃貶右庶子。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi strongly pleaded for him, and he was demoted to Right Companion of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi strongly pleaded for him, and he was demoted to Right Companion of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 裴約遣間使告急於帝，帝曰：「吾兄不幸，乃生梟獍，裴約獨能知逆順。」

translations.literal: Pei Yue sent secret messengers to report the emergency to the emperor; the emperor said, "My elder brother was unfortunate indeed to have raised such a wicked son; only Pei Yue knows right from rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yue sent secret messengers to report the emergency to the emperor. The emperor said, "My elder brother was unfortunate indeed to have raised such a wicked son; only Pei Yue knows right from rebellion.

sentences.zh: 顧謂北京內牙馬步軍都指揮使李紹斌曰：「澤州彈丸之地，朕無所用，卿為我取裴約以來。」

translations.literal: He turned to the northern capital's inner-gate horse-and-foot commanding officer Li Shaobin and said, "Ze Prefecture is a place no bigger than a pellet—I have no use for it. You fetch Pei Yue for me.
translations.idiomatic: He turned to the northern capital's inner-gate horse-and-foot commanding officer Li Shaobin and said, "Ze Prefecture is a place no bigger than a pellet—I have no use for it. You fetch Pei Yue for me.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬申，紹斌將甲士五千救之，未至，城已陷，約死。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on renshen, Shaobin led five thousand armored soldiers to the rescue, but before he arrived the city had already fallen and Yue died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renshen, Shaobin led five thousand armored soldiers to the rescue, but before he arrived the city had already fallen and Yue died.

sentences.zh: 帝深惜之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply mourned him.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，帝自楊劉還興唐。

translations.literal: On jiaxu the emperor returned from Yangliu to Xingtang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu the emperor returned from Yangliu to Xingtang.

sentences.zh: 梁主命於滑州決河，東注曹、濮及鄆以限唐兵。

translations.literal: The Liang emperor ordered the Yellow River breached at Hua Prefecture so it would flow east into Cao, Pu, and Yan to block Tang troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor ordered the Yellow River breached at Hua Prefecture so it would flow east into Cao, Pu, and Yan to block Tang troops.

sentences.zh: 初，梁主遣段凝監大軍於河上，敬翔、李振屢請罷之，梁主曰：「凝未有過。」

translations.literal: Initially the Liang emperor had sent Duan Ning to supervise the great army on the river; Jing Xiang and Li Zhen repeatedly asked that he be removed; the Liang emperor said, "Ning has not yet done wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Initially the Liang emperor had sent Duan Ning to supervise the great army on the river. Jing Xiang and Li Zhen repeatedly asked that he be removed, but the Liang emperor said, "Ning has not yet done wrong.

sentences.zh: 振曰：「俟其有過，則社稷危矣。」

translations.literal: Zhen said, "Wait until he does wrong and the altars of state will be in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said, "Wait until he does wrong and the altars of state will be in peril.

sentences.zh: 至是，凝厚賂趙、張求為招討使，翔、振力爭以為不可；

translations.literal: At this Ning lavishly bribed Zhao and Zhang to become campaign commissioner; Xiang and Zhen strongly argued against it;
translations.idiomatic: At this Ning lavishly bribed Zhao and Zhang to become campaign commissioner. Xiang and Zhen strongly argued against it;

sentences.zh: 趙、張主之，竟代王彥章為北面招討使，於是宿將憤怒，士卒亦不服，天下兵馬副元帥張宗奭言於梁主曰：「臣為副元帥，雖衰朽，猶足為陛下扞御北方。

translations.literal: Zhao and Zhang backed him and in the end he replaced Wang Yanzhang as northern campaign commissioner; veteran generals were furious and soldiers too would not obey; Deputy Overall Commander of All Troops Zhang Zongshi said to the Liang emperor, "Your subject serves as deputy overall commander—though aged, I am still enough to defend the north for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao and Zhang backed him, and in the end he replaced Wang Yanzhang as northern campaign commissioner. Veteran generals were furious and the soldiers would not obey. Deputy Overall Commander of All Troops Zhang Zongshi said to the Liang emperor, "Your subject serves as deputy overall commander—though aged, I am still enough to defend the north for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 段凝晚進，功名未能服人，眾議哅哅，恐貽國家深憂。」

translations.literal: Duan Ning is a latecomer whose achievements cannot command respect; public opinion is in an uproar—I fear deep trouble for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ning is a latecomer whose achievements cannot command respect. Public opinion is in an uproar, and I fear deep trouble for the state.

sentences.zh: 敬翔曰：「將帥系國安危，今國勢已爾，陛下豈可尚不留意邪！」

translations.literal: Jing Xiang said, "Generals and commanders bear on the state's safety and peril—now that the state's position is already thus, how can Your Majesty still not pay heed!
translations.idiomatic: Jing Xiang said, "Generals and commanders bear on the state's safety and peril. Now that the state's position is already thus, how can Your Majesty still not pay heed!

sentences.zh: 梁主皆不聽。

translations.literal: The Liang emperor would not listen to any of them.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor would not listen to any of them.

sentences.zh: 戊子，凝將全軍五萬營於王村，自高陵津濟河，剽掠澶州諸縣，至於頓丘。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Ning led the entire army of fifty thousand and encamped at Wang Village; from Gaoling Ford he crossed the river and raided the counties of Cang Prefecture as far as Dunqiu.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Ning led the entire army of fifty thousand and encamped at Wang Village. From Gaoling Ford he crossed the river and raided the counties of Cang Prefecture as far as Dunqiu.

sentences.zh: 梁主又命王彥章將保鑾騎士及它兵合萬人，屯兗、鄆之境，謀復鄆州，以張漢傑監其軍。

translations.literal: The Liang emperor also ordered Wang Yanzhang to lead the imperial guard cavalry and other troops totaling ten thousand, encamp on the border of Yanzhou and Yan Prefecture, and plan to recover Yan Prefecture, with Zhang Hanjie supervising his army.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor also ordered Wang Yanzhang to lead the imperial guard cavalry and other troops totaling ten thousand to encamp on the border of Yanzhou and Yan Prefecture and plan to recover Yan Prefecture, with Zhang Hanjie supervising his army.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，帝引兵屯朝城。

translations.literal: On gengyin the emperor led troops and encamped at Chaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin the emperor led troops and encamped at Chaocheng.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，康延孝帥百餘騎來奔，帝解所御錦袍玉帶賜之，以為南面招討都指揮使，領博州刺史。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Kang Yanxiao came in flight with more than a hundred horsemen; the emperor removed his own brocade robe and jade belt and bestowed them on him, making him southern campaign overall commanding officer and concurrent prefect of Bo.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Kang Yanxiao came over with more than a hundred horsemen. The emperor removed his own brocade robe and jade belt and bestowed them on him, appointing him southern campaign overall commanding officer and concurrent prefect of Bo.

sentences.zh: 帝屏人問延孝以梁事，對曰：「梁朝地不為狹，兵不為少；

translations.literal: The emperor dismissed attendants and questioned Yanxiao about Liang affairs; he replied, "The Liang dynasty's territory is not narrow and its troops are not few;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismissed attendants and questioned Yanxiao about Liang affairs. He replied, "The Liang dynasty's territory is not narrow and its troops are not few;

sentences.zh: 然跡其行事，終必敗亡。

translations.literal: yet tracing its conduct, it will in the end be defeated and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: yet judging by its conduct, it will in the end be defeated and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 主既暗懦，趙、張兄弟擅權，內結宮掖，外納貨賂，官之高下唯視賂之多少，不擇才德，不校勳勞。

translations.literal: The ruler is both dim and weak; the Zhao and Zhang brothers monopolize power, bind themselves within the palace harem and take bribes without, rank high or low depending only on how much is paid—neither talent nor virtue is chosen, neither merit nor toil is weighed.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler is both dim and weak. The Zhao and Zhang brothers monopolize power, bind themselves to the palace harem and take bribes from outside. Rank high or low depends only on how much is paid—neither talent nor virtue is chosen, neither merit nor toil is weighed.

sentences.zh: 段凝智勇俱無，一旦居王彥章、霍彥威之右，自將兵以來，專率斂行伍以奉權貴。

translations.literal: Duan Ning has neither wisdom nor courage; suddenly he stands above Wang Yanzhang and Huo Yanwei, and since taking command of troops he has devoted himself to squeezing the ranks to serve the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ning has neither wisdom nor courage, yet suddenly he stands above Wang Yanzhang and Huo Yanwei. Since taking command of troops he has devoted himself to squeezing the ranks to serve the powerful.

sentences.zh: 梁主每出一軍，不能專任將帥，常以近臣監之，進止可否動為所制。

translations.literal: Whenever the Liang emperor sends out an army he cannot fully entrust the generals and commanders—he always sends close ministers to supervise them, and advance, halt, approval, or refusal are constantly controlled by them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Liang emperor sends out an army he cannot fully entrust the generals and commanders. He always sends close ministers to supervise them, and advance, halt, approval, or refusal are constantly controlled by them.

sentences.zh: 近又聞欲數道出兵，令董璋引陝虢、澤潞之兵自石會關趣太原，霍彥威以汝、洛之兵自相衛、邢洺寇鎮定，王彥章、張漢傑以禁軍攻鄆州，段凝、杜晏球以大軍當陛下，決以十月大舉。

translations.literal: Recently I also heard they intend to send troops on several routes: Dong Zhang to lead Shaan-Guo and Ze-Lu troops from Shihui Pass toward Taiyuan; Huo Yanwei with Ru-Luo troops from Xiangwei and Xing-Mo to raid Zhen-Ding; Wang Yanzhang and Zhang Hanjie with the imperial guard to attack Yan Prefecture; Duan Ning and Du Yanqiu with the great army to face Your Majesty—they have decided on a major campaign in the tenth month.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I also heard they intend to send troops on several routes: Dong Zhang to lead Shaan-Guo and Ze-Lu troops from Shihui Pass toward Taiyuan; Huo Yanwei with Ru-Luo troops from Xiangwei and Xing-Mo to raid Zhen-Ding; Wang Yanzhang and Zhang Hanjie with the imperial guard to attack Yan Prefecture; Duan Ning and Du Yanqiu with the great army to face Your Majesty. They have decided on a major campaign in the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 臣竊觀梁兵聚則不少，分則不多。

translations.literal: Your subject observes in private that when Liang troops are gathered they are not few, but when divided they are not many.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that when Liang troops are gathered they are not few, but when divided they are not many.

sentences.zh: 願陛下養勇蓄力以待其分兵，帥精騎五千自鄆州直抵大梁，擒其偽主，旬月之間，天下定矣。」

translations.literal: I ask Your Majesty to nurture courage and store strength while waiting for them to divide their forces, then lead five thousand picked cavalry straight from Yan Prefecture to Liang, seize their false ruler, and within a month or so the realm will be settled.
translations.idiomatic: I ask Your Majesty to nurture courage and store strength while waiting for them to divide their forces, then lead five thousand picked cavalry straight from Yan Prefecture to Liang, seize their false ruler, and within a month or so the realm will be settled.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 蜀主以文思殿大學士韓昭、內皇城使潘在迎、武勇軍使顧在珣為狎客，陪侍游宴，與宮女雜坐，或為艷歌相唱和，或談嘲謔浪，鄙俚褻慢，無所不至，蜀主樂之。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler made Wensi Hall Academician Han Zhao, Inner Imperial City Commissioner Pan Zaiying, and Wuyong Army Commissioner Gu Zaiqun his intimate companions; they attended his tours and banquets, sat mixed with palace women, sometimes sang sensual songs in turn, sometimes traded jokes and coarse banter—vulgar, lewd, and disrespectful without limit—and the Shu ruler delighted in it.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler made Wensi Hall Academician Han Zhao, Inner Imperial City Commissioner Pan Zaiying, and Wuyong Army Commissioner Gu Zaiqun his intimate companions. They attended his tours and banquets, sat mixed with palace women, sometimes sang sensual songs in turn, sometimes traded jokes and coarse banter—vulgar, lewd, and disrespectful without limit—and the Shu ruler delighted in it.

sentences.zh: 在珣，彥朗之子也。

translations.literal: Zaiqun was the son of Yanlang.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiqun was the son of Yanlang.

sentences.zh: 時樞密使宋光嗣等專斷國家，恣為威虐，務徇蜀主之欲以盜其權。

translations.literal: At this time Palace Secretariat Commissioner Song Guangsi and others monopolized state affairs, indulged in tyranny at will, and strove to satisfy the Shu ruler's desires in order to usurp his power.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Palace Secretariat Commissioner Song Guangsi and others monopolized state affairs, indulged in tyranny at will, and strove to satisfy the Shu ruler's desires in order to usurp his power.

sentences.zh: 宰相王鍇、庾傳素等各保寵祿，無敢規正。

translations.literal: Grand Councillors Wang Kai, Yu Chuansu, and the rest each preserved their favor and stipends and none dared remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councillors Wang Kai, Yu Chuansu, and the rest each preserved their favor and stipends, and none dared remonstrate.

sentences.zh: 潘在迎每勸蜀主誅諫者，無使謗國。

translations.literal: Pan Zaiying often urged the Shu ruler to execute remonstrators so the state would not be slandered.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Zaiying often urged the Shu ruler to execute remonstrators so the state would not be slandered.

sentences.zh: 嘉州司馬劉贊獻陳後主三閣圖，並作歌以諷；

translations.literal: Jia Prefecture aide Liu Zan presented a painting of the Later Chen ruler's Three Pavilions and also composed a song to satirize it;
translations.idiomatic: Jia Prefecture aide Liu Zan presented a painting of the Later Chen ruler's Three Pavilions and also composed a song to satirize it;

sentences.zh: 賢良方正蒲禹卿對策語極切直；

translations.literal: the Worthy and Upright candidate Pu Yuqing answered the examination with words extremely blunt and direct;
translations.idiomatic: the Worthy and Upright candidate Pu Yuqing answered the examination with words extremely blunt and direct;

sentences.zh: 蜀主雖不罪，亦不能用也。

translations.literal: the Shu ruler though he did not punish them, also could not employ them.
translations.idiomatic: the Shu ruler did not punish them, but he also could not employ them.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚戌，蜀主以重陽宴近臣於宣華宛，酒酣，嘉王宗壽乘間極言社稷將危，流涕不已。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on gengxu, the Shu ruler held a Double Ninth banquet for close ministers at Xuanhua Park; when the wine was deep, Prince Jia Zongshou seized the moment and spoke at length that the altars of state were about to be in peril, weeping without cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on gengxu, the Shu ruler held a Double Ninth banquet for close ministers at Xuanhua Park. When the wine was deep, Prince Jia Zongshou seized the moment and spoke at length that the altars of state were about to be in peril, weeping without cease.

sentences.zh: 韓昭、潘在迎曰：「嘉王好酒悲。」

translations.literal: Han Zhao and Pan Zaiying said, "Prince Jia loves wine and grows sorrowful.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zhao and Pan Zaiying said, "Prince Jia loves wine and grows sorrowful.

sentences.zh: 因諧笑而罷。

translations.literal: With jesting laughter they ended it.
translations.idiomatic: With jesting laughter they ended it.

sentences.zh: 帝在朝城，梁段凝進至臨河之南，澶西、相南，日有寇掠。

translations.literal: The emperor was at Chaocheng; Liang's Duan Ning advanced to the south of Linhe, west of Cang and south of Xiang, with daily raids.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was at Chaocheng. Liang's Duan Ning advanced to the south of Linhe, west of Cang and south of Xiang, with daily raids.

sentences.zh: 自德勝失利以來，喪芻糧數百萬，租庸副使孔謙暴斂以供軍，民多流亡，租稅益少，倉廩之積不支半歲。

translations.literal: Since the defeat at Desheng, fodder and grain lost ran to millions; Rent and Corvée Deputy Commissioner Kong Qian levied harshly to supply the army; the people fled in great numbers; rent and tax grew ever less; storehouse reserves would not last half a year.
translations.idiomatic: Since the defeat at Desheng, fodder and grain lost ran to millions. Rent and Corvée Deputy Commissioner Kong Qian levied harshly to supply the army, the people fled in great numbers, rent and tax grew ever less, and storehouse reserves would not last half a year.

sentences.zh: 澤潞未下。

translations.literal: Ze and Lu had not yet been taken.
translations.idiomatic: Ze and Lu had not yet been taken.

sentences.zh: 盧文進、王郁引契丹屢過瀛、涿之南，傳聞俟草枯冰合，深入為寇。

translations.literal: Lu Wenjin and Wang Yu led Khitan forces repeatedly south of Ying and Zhuo; rumor held they awaited withered grass and frozen ice to raid deep.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wenjin and Wang Yu led Khitan forces repeatedly south of Ying and Zhuo. Rumor held they were waiting for withered grass and frozen ice to raid deep.

sentences.zh: 又聞梁人欲大舉數道入寇，帝深以為憂，召諸將會議。

translations.literal: He also heard Liang troops intended a major campaign on several routes to invade; the emperor was deeply troubled and summoned the generals to confer.
translations.idiomatic: He also heard Liang troops intended a major campaign on several routes to invade. The emperor was deeply troubled and summoned the generals to confer.

sentences.zh: 宣徽使李紹宏等皆以為鄆州城門之外皆為寇境，孤遠難守，有之不如無之，請以易衛州及黎陽於梁，與之約和，以河為境，休兵息民，俟財力稍集，更圖後舉。

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Commissioner Li Shaohong and the rest all held that beyond Yan Prefecture's gates lay nothing but enemy territory—lonely, distant, and hard to hold—better not to have it than to have it; they asked to exchange it with Wei Prefecture and Liyang for Liang, make peace with them, take the river as border, rest troops and soothe the people, wait until wealth and strength were somewhat gathered, and plan a later campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretariat Commissioner Li Shaohong and the rest all held that beyond Yan Prefecture's gates lay nothing but enemy territory—lonely, distant, and hard to hold—better not to have it than to have it. They asked to exchange it with Wei Prefecture and Liyang for Liang, make peace with them, take the river as border, rest troops and soothe the people, wait until wealth and strength were somewhat gathered, and plan a later campaign.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅，曰：「如此吾無葬地矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and said, "If it comes to this I shall have no place for burial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and said, "If it comes to this I shall have no place for burial.

sentences.zh: 乃罷諸將，獨召郭崇韜問之。

translations.literal: He dismissed the generals and summoned Guo Chongtao alone to question him.
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed the generals and summoned Guo Chongtao alone to question him.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下不櫛沐，不解甲，十五餘年，其志欲以雪家國之仇恥也。

translations.literal: He replied, "Your Majesty has not washed your hair, has not removed your armor, for more than fifteen years—your will has been to wipe away the family and state's shame and humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Your Majesty has not washed your hair or removed your armor for more than fifteen years. Your will has been to wipe away the family and state's shame and humiliation.

sentences.zh: 今已正尊號，河北士庶日望昇平，始得鄆州尺寸之地，不能守而棄之，安能盡有中原乎！

translations.literal: Now you have taken the proper title; the gentry and commoners north of the Yellow River daily look for peace; you have only just gained a scrap of land at Yan Prefecture—if you cannot hold it and abandon it, how can you fully possess the Central Plain!
translations.idiomatic: Now you have taken the proper title. The gentry and commoners north of the Yellow River daily look for peace. You have only just gained a scrap of land at Yan Prefecture—if you cannot hold it and abandon it, how can you fully possess the Central Plain!

sentences.zh: 臣恐將士解體，將來食盡眾散，雖畫河為境，誰為陛下守之！

translations.literal: Your subject fears the officers and soldiers will lose heart; when food runs out the masses will scatter; even if the river is drawn as border, who will hold it for Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: I fear the officers and soldiers will lose heart. When food runs out the masses will scatter. Even if the river is drawn as border, who will hold it for Your Majesty!

sentences.zh: 臣嘗細詢康延孝以河南之事，度已料彼，日夜思之，成敗之機決在今歲。

translations.literal: Your subject once questioned Kang Yanxiao in detail about affairs south of the Yellow River; having measured and already anticipated them, I think on it day and night—the moment of success or failure will be decided this year.
translations.idiomatic: I once questioned Kang Yanxiao in detail about affairs south of the Yellow River. Having measured and already anticipated them, I think on it day and night—the moment of success or failure will be decided this year.

sentences.zh: 梁今悉以精兵授段凝，據我南鄙，又決河自固，謂我猝不能渡，恃此不復為備。

translations.literal: Liang now gives all its picked troops to Duan Ning to hold our southern frontier; it has also breached the river to secure itself, thinking we cannot cross in haste and relying on this no longer to prepare.
translations.idiomatic: Liang now gives all its picked troops to Duan Ning to hold our southern frontier. It has also breached the river to secure itself, thinking we cannot cross in haste and relying on this no longer to prepare.

sentences.zh: 使王彥章侵逼鄆州，其意冀有奸人動搖，變生於內耳。

translations.literal: It sends Wang Yanzhang to press Yan Prefecture—its intent is to hope for traitors to waver and change to arise within.
translations.idiomatic: It sends Wang Yanzhang to press Yan Prefecture—its intent is to hope for traitors to waver and rebellion to arise within.

sentences.zh: 段凝本非將材，不能臨機決策，無足可畏。

translations.literal: Duan Ning is by nature no general's material; he cannot decide on the spur of the moment—there is nothing to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ning is by nature no general's material. He cannot decide on the spur of the moment—there is nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 降者皆言大梁無兵，陛下若留兵守魏，固保楊劉，自以精兵與鄆州合勢，長驅入汴，彼城中既空虛，必望風自潰。

translations.literal: Defectors all say Liang has no troops; if Your Majesty leaves troops to hold Wei, firmly secures Yangliu, and yourself leads picked troops to join forces with Yan Prefecture and drive straight into Bian, their city being already empty will surely collapse at the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Defectors all say Liang has no troops. If Your Majesty leaves troops to hold Wei, firmly secures Yangliu, and yourself leads picked troops to join forces with Yan Prefecture and drive straight into Bian, their city being already empty will surely collapse at the first blow.

sentences.zh: 苟偽主授首，則諸將自降矣。

translations.literal: If the false ruler offers his head, the generals will surrender of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: If the false ruler offers his head, the generals will surrender of themselves.

sentences.zh: 不然，今秋谷不登，軍糧將盡，若非陛下決志，大功何由可成！

translations.literal: Otherwise, this autumn the grain will not ripen and army provisions will run out—if not for Your Majesty's resolute will, how can the great achievement be accomplished!
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, this autumn the grain will not ripen and army provisions will run out. Without Your Majesty's resolute will, how can the great achievement be accomplished!

sentences.zh: 諺曰：『當道築室，三年不成。』

translations.literal: A proverb says, 'Build a house in the road and in three years it will not be finished.
translations.idiomatic: A proverb says, 'Build a house in the road and in three years it will not be finished.

sentences.zh: 帝王應運，必有天命，在陛下勿疑耳。」

translations.literal: A ruler who answers to the age must have Heaven's mandate—it rests with Your Majesty not to doubt."
translations.idiomatic: A ruler who answers to the age must have Heaven's mandate—it rests with Your Majesty not to doubt."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此正合朕志。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "This exactly matches my will.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "This exactly matches my will.

sentences.zh: 丈夫得則為王，失則為虜，吾行決矣！」

translations.literal: A man who wins becomes king, who loses becomes captive—I am resolved to act!"
translations.idiomatic: A man who wins becomes king, who loses becomes captive—I am resolved to act!"

sentences.zh: 司天奏：「今歲天道不利，深入必無功。」

translations.literal: The Bureau of Astronomy reported, "This year the heavenly way is unfavorable; a deep advance will surely achieve nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Astronomy reported, "This year the heavens are unfavorable; a deep advance will surely achieve nothing.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 王彥章引兵逾汶水，將攻鄆州，李嗣源遣李從珂將騎兵逆戰，敗其前鋒於遞坊鎮，獲將士三百人，斬首二百級，彥章退保中都。

translations.literal: Wang Yanzhang led troops across the Wen River, intending to attack Yan Prefecture; Li Siyuan sent Li Congke to lead cavalry to meet him in battle, defeated his vanguard at Difang Town, captured three hundred officers and soldiers, took two hundred heads, and Yanzhang withdrew to hold Zhongdu.
