translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanzhang led troops across the Wen River, intending to attack Yan Prefecture. Li Siyuan sent Li Congke to lead cavalry against him, defeated his vanguard at Difang Town, captured three hundred officers and soldiers, and took two hundred heads. Yanzhang withdrew to hold Zhongdu.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，捷奏至朝城，帝大喜，謂郭崇韜曰：「鄆州告捷，足壯吾氣！」

translations.literal: On wuchen the victory report reached Chaocheng; the emperor was greatly pleased and said to Guo Chongtao, "Yan Prefecture reports victory—enough to strengthen my spirits!
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen the victory report reached Chaocheng. The emperor was greatly pleased and said to Guo Chongtao, "Yan Prefecture reports victory—that is enough to lift my spirits!

sentences.zh: 己巳，命將士悉遣其家歸興唐。

translations.literal: On jisi he ordered the officers and soldiers to send all their families back to Xingtang.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi he ordered the officers and soldiers to send all their families back to Xingtang.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛未朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day xinwei, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day xinwei, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 帝遣魏國夫人劉氏、皇子繼岌歸興唐，與之訣曰：「事之成敗，在此一決。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Lady Liu of Wei and the prince Jiji back to Xingtang, and taking leave of them said, "Success or failure in this affair will be decided in this one move.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Lady Liu of Wei and Prince Jiji back to Xingtang, and taking leave of them said, "Success or failure in this affair will be decided in this one stroke.

sentences.zh: 若其不濟，當聚吾家於魏宮而焚之！」

translations.literal: If it does not succeed, you must gather my family in the Wei palace and burn them!
translations.idiomatic: If it does not succeed, gather my family in the Wei palace and burn them!

sentences.zh: 仍命豆盧革、李紹宏、張憲、王正言同守東京。

translations.literal: He also ordered Doulu Ge, Li Shaohong, Zhang Xian, and Wang Zhengyan jointly to hold Dongjing.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Doulu Ge, Li Shaohong, Zhang Xian, and Wang Zhengyan jointly to hold Dongjing.

sentences.zh: 壬申，帝以大軍自楊劉濟河，癸酉，至鄆州，中夜，進軍逾汶，以李嗣源為前鋒，甲戌旦，遇梁兵，一戰敗之，追至中都，圍其城。

translations.literal: On renshen the emperor led the great army from Yangliu across the river; on guiyou he reached Yan Prefecture; in the middle of the night he advanced the army across the Wen; he made Li Siyuan vanguard; at dawn on jiaxu he met Liang troops, defeated them in one battle, pursued to Zhongdu, and besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen the emperor led the great army from Yangliu across the river. On guiyou he reached Yan Prefecture, and in the middle of the night advanced across the Wen with Li Siyuan as vanguard. At dawn on jiaxu he met Liang troops, defeated them in one battle, pursued to Zhongdu, and besieged the city.

sentences.zh: 城無守備，少頃，梁兵潰圍出，追擊，破之。

translations.literal: The city had no defenses; before long Liang troops burst through the encirclement and fled; Tang pursued and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: The city had no defenses. Before long Liang troops burst through the encirclement and fled. Tang forces pursued and broke them.

sentences.zh: 王彥章以數十騎走，龍武大將軍李紹奇單騎追之，識其聲，曰：「王鐵槍也！」

translations.literal: Wang Yanzhang fled with several dozen horsemen; Longwu Grand General Li Shaoqi pursued alone, recognized his voice, and said, "Iron Spear Wang!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanzhang fled with several dozen horsemen. Longwu Grand General Li Shaoqi pursued alone, recognized his voice, and cried, "Iron Spear Wang!

sentences.zh: 拔槊刺之，彥章重傷，馬躓，遂擒之，並擒都監張漢傑、曹州刺史李知節、裨將趙廷隱、劉嗣彬等二百餘人，斬首數千級。

translations.literal: He pulled his spear and thrust at him; Yanzhang was gravely wounded, his horse stumbled, and he was captured, along with Army Supervisor Zhang Hanjie, Cao Prefecture prefect Li Zhijie, staff generals Zhao Tingyin, Liu Sibin, and more than two hundred others; heads taken numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He pulled his spear and thrust at him. Yanzhang was gravely wounded, his horse stumbled, and he was captured, along with Army Supervisor Zhang Hanjie, Cao Prefecture prefect Li Zhijie, staff generals Zhao Tingyin, Liu Sibin, and more than two hundred others. Heads taken numbered in the thousands.

sentences.zh: 廷隱，開封人；

translations.literal: Tingyin was a man of Kaifeng;
translations.idiomatic: Tingyin was a man of Kaifeng;

sentences.zh: 嗣彬，知俊之族子也。

translations.literal: Sibin was a clansman of Zhijun.
translations.idiomatic: Sibin was a clansman of Li Zhijun.

sentences.zh: 彥章嘗謂人曰：「李亞子鬥雞小兒，何足畏！」

translations.literal: Yanzhang had once said to people, "Li Yazi is a cockfighting boy—what is there to fear!
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhang had once said to people, "Li Yazi is a cockfighting boy—what is there to fear!

sentences.zh: 至是，帝謂彥章曰：「爾常謂我小兒，今日服未？」

translations.literal: At this the emperor said to Yanzhang, "You always called me a boy—are you convinced today?
translations.idiomatic: At this the emperor said to Yanzhang, "You always called me a boy—are you convinced now?

sentences.zh: 又問：「爾名善將，何不守兗州？

translations.literal: He asked again, "You are famed as a capable general—why did you not hold Yanzhou?
translations.idiomatic: He asked again, "You are famed as a capable general—why did you not hold Yanzhou?

sentences.zh: 中都無壁壘，何以自固？」

translations.literal: Zhongdu had no walls or ramparts—how could you secure yourself?
translations.idiomatic: Zhongdu had no walls or ramparts—how could you hold yourself there?

sentences.zh: 彥章對曰：「天命已去，無足言者。」

translations.literal: Yanzhang replied, "Heaven's mandate is already gone—there is nothing worth saying.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhang replied, "Heaven's mandate is already gone—there is nothing worth saying.

sentences.zh: 帝惜彥章之材，欲用之，賜藥傅其創，屢遣人誘諭之。

translations.literal: The emperor valued Yanzhang's talent and wished to employ him; he gave him medicine and dressed his wounds and repeatedly sent men to persuade him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor valued Yanzhang's talent and wished to employ him. He gave him medicine and dressed his wounds and repeatedly sent men to persuade him.

sentences.zh: 彥章曰：「余本匹夫，蒙梁恩，位至上將，與皇帝交戰十五年；

translations.literal: Yanzhang said, "I was originally a common man; I received Liang's grace and rose to grand general; I have fought the emperor for fifteen years;
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhang said, "I was originally a common man. I received Liang's grace and rose to grand general. I have fought the emperor for fifteen years;

sentences.zh: 今兵敗力窮，死自其分，縱皇帝憐而生我，我何面目見天下之人乎！

translations.literal: Now my army is defeated and my strength exhausted—death is my due; even if the emperor pities me and lets me live, with what face could I meet the people of the realm!
translations.idiomatic: Now my army is defeated and my strength exhausted—death is my due. Even if the emperor pities me and lets me live, with what face could I meet the people of the realm!

sentences.zh: 豈有朝為梁將，暮為唐臣！

translations.literal: How could one be a Liang general in the morning and a Tang subject at evening!
translations.idiomatic: How could one be a Liang general in the morning and a Tang subject by evening!

sentences.zh: 此我所不為也。」

translations.literal: This is what I will not do.
translations.idiomatic: This is what I will not do.

sentences.zh: 帝復遣李嗣源自往諭之，彥章臥謂嗣源曰：「汝非邈佶烈乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor again sent Li Siyuan to persuade him in person; Yanzhang, lying down, said to Siyuan, "Are you not Yaojilie?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again sent Li Siyuan to persuade him in person. Yanzhang, lying down, said to Siyuan, "Are you not Yaojilie?

sentences.zh: 彥章素輕嗣源，故以小名呼之。

translations.literal: Yanzhang had always looked down on Siyuan, so he called him by his childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhang had always looked down on Siyuan, so he called him by his childhood name.

sentences.zh: 於是諸將稱賀，帝舉酒屬李嗣源曰：「今日之功，公與崇韜之力也。

translations.literal: Then the generals offered congratulations; the emperor raised his cup and turned to Li Siyuan, saying, "Today's achievement is the work of you and Chongtao.
translations.idiomatic: Then the generals offered congratulations. The emperor raised his cup and turned to Li Siyuan, saying, "Today's achievement is the work of you and Chongtao.

sentences.zh: 曏從紹宏輩語，大事去矣。」

translations.literal: Earlier when I listened to Shaohong and his crowd, the great affair was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when I listened to Shaohong and his crowd, the great affair was lost.

sentences.zh: 帝又謂諸將曰：「曏所患惟王彥章，今已就擒，是天意滅梁也。

translations.literal: The emperor also said to the generals, "What I feared before was only Wang Yanzhang; now he is captured—it is Heaven's will to destroy Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also said to the generals, "What I feared before was only Wang Yanzhang. Now he is captured—it is Heaven's will to destroy Liang.

sentences.zh: 段凝猶在河上，進退之計，宜何向而可？」

translations.literal: Duan Ning is still north of the river; as for the plan of advance or retreat, which direction should we take?
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ning is still north of the river. As for whether to advance or retreat, which direction should we take?

sentences.zh: 諸將以為；

translations.literal: The generals held that;
translations.idiomatic: The generals held that;

sentences.zh: 「傳者雖雲大梁無備，未知虛實。

translations.literal: Reports say Daliang has no defenses, but we do not know whether that is true or false.
translations.idiomatic: Reports say Daliang has no defenses, but we do not know whether that is true or false.

sentences.zh: 今東方諸鎮兵皆在段凝麾下，所餘空城耳，以陛下天威臨之，無不下者。

translations.literal: Now all the troops of the eastern commanderies are under Duan Ning; what remains are empty cities; with Your Majesty's majesty pressing upon them, none will fail to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Now all the troops of the eastern commanderies are under Duan Ning; what remains are empty cities. With Your Majesty's majesty pressing upon them, none will fail to submit.

sentences.zh: 若先廣地，東傅於海，然後觀釁而動，可以萬全。」

translations.literal: If we first spread our territory east until it reaches the sea and then watch for openings to act, we can be entirely secure.
translations.idiomatic: If we first spread our territory east until it reaches the sea and then watch for openings to act, we can be entirely secure.

sentences.zh: 康延孝固請亟取大梁。

translations.literal: Kang Yanxiao firmly urged taking Daliang at once.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Yanxiao firmly urged taking Daliang at once.

sentences.zh: 李嗣源曰：「兵貴神速。

translations.literal: Li Siyuan said, "In war, speed is prized.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siyuan said, "In war, speed is prized.

sentences.zh: 今彥章就擒，段凝必未之知；

translations.literal: Now Yanzhang is captured—Duan Ning surely does not yet know;
translations.idiomatic: Now Yanzhang is captured—Duan Ning surely does not yet know;

sentences.zh: 就使有人走告，疑信之間尚須三日。

translations.literal: Even if someone ran to tell him, between doubt and belief three days would still be required.
translations.idiomatic: Even if someone ran to tell him, between doubt and belief three days would still be required.

sentences.zh: 設若知吾所向，即發救兵，直路則阻決河，須自白馬南渡，數萬之眾，舟楫亦難猝辦。

translations.literal: Suppose he knew where we were headed and dispatched rescue troops—the direct route would be blocked by the breached river; they would have to cross south from Baima; for a force of tens of thousands, boats would be hard to prepare at once.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose he knew where we were headed and dispatched rescue troops—the direct route would be blocked by the breached river. They would have to cross south from Baima, and for a force of tens of thousands, boats would be hard to prepare at once.

sentences.zh: 此去大梁至近，前無山險，方陳橫行，晝夜兼程，信宿可至。

translations.literal: From here to Daliang is extremely near; there are no mountain barriers ahead; form the ranks and march unopposed—day and night at forced march, we could arrive in two overnight stops.
translations.idiomatic: From here to Daliang is extremely near, and there are no mountain barriers ahead. Form the ranks and march unopposed—day and night at forced march, we could arrive in two overnight stops.

sentences.zh: 段凝未離河上，友貞已為吾擒矣。

translations.literal: Before Duan Ning leaves the north bank of the river, Youzhen will already be in our hands.
translations.idiomatic: Before Duan Ning leaves the north bank of the river, Youzhen will already be in our hands.

sentences.zh: 延孝之言是也，請陛下以大軍徐進，臣願以千騎前驅。」

translations.literal: Yanxiao's words are correct; I ask Your Majesty to advance the great army at a steady pace while I wish to take a thousand horsemen as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxiao's words are correct. I ask Your Majesty to advance the great army at a steady pace while I take a thousand horsemen as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 令下，諸軍皆踴躍願行。

translations.literal: When the order was issued, all the armies leaped with joy and wished to march.
translations.idiomatic: When the order was issued, all the armies leaped with joy and wished to march.

sentences.zh: 是夕，嗣源帥前軍倍道趣大梁。

translations.literal: That evening Siyuan led the advance army by double marches toward Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: That evening Siyuan led the advance army by forced marches toward Daliang.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，帝發中都，舁王彥章自隨，遣中使問彥章曰：「吾此行克乎？」

translations.literal: On yihai the emperor set out from Zhongdu with Wang Yanzhang carried along and sent a palace envoy to ask Yanzhang, "Will I succeed on this expedition?
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the emperor set out from Zhongdu with Wang Yanzhang carried along and sent a palace envoy to ask Yanzhang, "Will I succeed on this expedition?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「段凝有精兵六萬，雖主將非材，亦未肯遽爾倒戈，殆難克也。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Duan Ning has sixty thousand picked troops; though the commander-in-chief is no great talent, they will not lightly turn their spears—it will be hard to overcome.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Duan Ning has sixty thousand picked troops. Though the commander-in-chief is no great talent, they will not lightly turn their spears—it will be hard to overcome.

sentences.zh: 帝知其終不為用，遂斬之。

translations.literal: The emperor knew he would never serve them and had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew he would never serve them and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，至曹州，梁守將降。

translations.literal: On dingchou they reached Cao Prefecture; the Liang defending general surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou they reached Cao Prefecture, and the Liang defending general surrendered.

sentences.zh: 王彥章敗卒有先至大梁，告梁主以「彥章就擒，唐軍長驅且至」者，梁主聚族哭曰：「運祚盡矣！」

translations.literal: Defeated soldiers of Wang Yanzhang had arrived at Daliang first and told the Liang emperor that Yanzhang had been captured and Tang troops were driving straight and would soon arrive; the Liang emperor gathered his clan and wept, saying, "Our fate is exhausted!
translations.idiomatic: Defeated soldiers of Wang Yanzhang had arrived at Daliang first and told the Liang emperor that Yanzhang had been captured and Tang troops were driving straight and would soon arrive. The Liang emperor gathered his clan and wept, saying, "Our fate is exhausted!

sentences.zh: 召群臣問策，皆莫能對。

translations.literal: He summoned the ministers to ask for plans; none could answer.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the ministers to ask for plans, but none could answer.

sentences.zh: 梁主謂敬翔曰：「朕居常忽卿所言，以至於此。

translations.literal: The Liang emperor said to Jing Xiang, "I usually neglected what you said, and it has come to this.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor said to Jing Xiang, "I usually neglected what you said, and it has come to this.

sentences.zh: 今事急矣，卿勿以為懟。

translations.literal: Now the affair is urgent—do not take offense.
translations.idiomatic: Now the affair is urgent—do not take offense.

sentences.zh: 將若之何？」

translations.literal: What are we to do?
translations.idiomatic: What are we to do?

sentences.zh: 翔泣曰：「臣受先帝厚恩，殆將三紀，名為宰相，其實朱氏老奴，事陛下如郎君。

translations.literal: Xiang wept and said, "Your subject received the late emperor's deep grace—nearly three decades have passed; though titled grand councilor, I am in truth an old servant of the Zhu clan, serving Your Majesty as a son might a father.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang wept and said, "Your subject received the late emperor's deep grace—nearly three decades have passed. Though titled grand councilor, I am in truth an old servant of the Zhu clan, serving Your Majesty as a son might a father.

sentences.zh: 臣前後獻言，莫匪盡忠。

translations.literal: The advice I offered before and after was nothing if not loyal.
translations.idiomatic: The advice I offered before and after was nothing if not loyal.

sentences.zh: 陛下初用段凝，臣極言不可，小人朋比，致有今日。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty first employed Duan Ning, I spoke most strongly against it; villains banded together and brought about today.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty first employed Duan Ning, I spoke most strongly against it. Villains banded together and brought about today.

sentences.zh: 今唐兵且至，段凝限於水北，不能赴救。

translations.literal: Now Tang troops will soon arrive; Duan Ning is confined north of the river and cannot come to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Now Tang troops will soon arrive. Duan Ning is confined north of the river and cannot come to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 臣欲請取下出居避狄，陛下必不聽從；

translations.literal: Your subject wishes to ask that you, the Son of Heaven, go out to dwell elsewhere and avoid disaster—Your Majesty will surely not listen;
translations.idiomatic: I wish to ask that Your Majesty leave the capital and dwell elsewhere to avoid disaster—Your Majesty will surely not listen;

sentences.zh: 欲請陛下出奇合戰，陛下必不果決。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes to ask Your Majesty to strike with a surprise force and join battle—Your Majesty will surely not decisively act.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to ask Your Majesty to strike with a surprise force and join battle—Your Majesty will surely not decisively act.

sentences.zh: 雖使良、平更生，誰能為陛下計者！

translations.literal: Even if Liang and Ping were reborn, who could devise a plan for Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: Even if Zhang Liang and Chen Ping were reborn, who could devise a plan for Your Majesty!

sentences.zh: 臣願先賜死，不忍見宗廟之亡也。」

translations.literal: Your subject asks first to be granted death—I cannot bear to see the ancestral temples perish.
translations.idiomatic: I ask first to be granted death—I cannot bear to see the ancestral temples perish.

sentences.zh: 因與梁主相向慟哭。

translations.literal: Then he and the Liang emperor wept facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: Then he and the Liang emperor wept facing each other.

sentences.zh: 梁主遣張漢倫馳騎追段凝軍。

translations.literal: The Liang emperor sent Zhang Hanlun at full gallop to overtake Duan Ning's army.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor sent Zhang Hanlun at full gallop to overtake Duan Ning's army.

sentences.zh: 漢倫至滑州，墜馬傷足，復限水不能進。

translations.literal: Hanlun reached Hua Prefecture, fell from his horse and injured his foot, and again was blocked by the river and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlun reached Hua Prefecture, fell from his horse and injured his foot, and again was blocked by the river and could not advance.

sentences.zh: 時城中尚有控鶴軍數千，朱珪請帥之出戰。

translations.literal: In the city there were still several thousand Crane-Control troops; Zhu Gui asked to lead them out to give battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the city there were still several thousand Crane-Control troops. Zhu Gui asked to lead them out to give battle.

sentences.zh: 梁主不從，命開封尹王瓚驅市人乘城為備。

translations.literal: The Liang emperor would not agree and ordered Kaifeng prefect Wang Zan to drive market people onto the walls to defend.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor would not agree and ordered Kaifeng prefect Wang Zan to drive market people onto the walls to defend.

sentences.zh: 初，梁陝州節度使邵王友誨，全昱之子也，性穎悟，人心多向之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liang's military commissioner of Shaanzhou, Prince of Shao Youhui, son of Quanyu, was quick-witted and men's hearts largely turned toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Liang's military commissioner of Shaanzhou, Prince of Shao Youhui, son of Quanyu, was quick-witted and men's hearts largely turned toward him.

sentences.zh: 或言其誘致禁軍欲為亂，梁主召還，與其兄友諒、友能並幽於別第。

translations.literal: Some said he had lured the forbidden army intending rebellion; the Liang emperor summoned him back and together with his older brothers Youliang and Youneng confined them in separate residences.
translations.idiomatic: Some said he had lured the forbidden army intending rebellion. The Liang emperor summoned him back and, together with his older brothers Youliang and Youneng, confined them in separate residences.

sentences.zh: 及唐師將至，梁主疑諸兄弟乘危謀亂，並皇弟賀王友雍、建王友徽盡殺之。

translations.literal: When Tang troops were about to arrive, the Liang emperor suspected the brothers might plot disorder in the crisis and together with Imperial younger brother Prince of He Youyong and Prince of Jian Youhui had them all killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang troops were about to arrive, the Liang emperor suspected the brothers might plot disorder in the crisis and, together with Imperial younger brother Prince of He Youyong and Prince of Jian Youhui, had them all killed.

sentences.zh: 梁主登建國樓，面擇親信厚賜之，使衣野服，繼蠟詔，促段凝軍，既辭，皆亡匿。

translations.literal: The Liang emperor ascended Jianguo Tower, personally chose trusted men and richly rewarded them, had them wear common clothes and carry sealed wax edicts urging Duan Ning's army; once they had taken leave, all fled and hid.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor ascended Jianguo Tower, personally chose trusted men and richly rewarded them, had them wear common clothes and carry sealed wax edicts urging Duan Ning's army, and once they had taken leave, all fled and hid.

sentences.zh: 或請幸洛陽，收集諸軍以拒唐，唐雖得都城，勢不能久留。

translations.literal: Some suggested going to Luoyang to gather the armies and resist Tang; though Tang might take the capital, it could not remain long.
translations.idiomatic: Some suggested going to Luoyang to gather the armies and resist Tang. Though Tang might take the capital, it could not remain long.

sentences.zh: 或請幸段凝軍，控鶴都指揮使皇甫麟曰：「凝本非將材，官由幸進，今危窘之際，望其臨機制勝，轉敗為功，難矣。

translations.literal: Some suggested going to Duan Ning's army; Crane-Control Commanding Officer Huangfu Lin said, "Ning by nature is no general's material; his office came through favor; in this moment of crisis, to expect him to seize the moment, turn defeat into victory—that is hard.
translations.idiomatic: Some suggested going to Duan Ning's army. Crane-Control Commanding Officer Huangfu Lin said, "Ning by nature is no general's material; his office came through favor. In this moment of crisis, to expect him to seize the moment and turn defeat into victory—that is hard.

sentences.zh: 且凝聞彥章軍敗，其膽已破，安知能終為陛下盡節乎！」

translations.literal: Moreover, when Ning hears Yanzhang's army was defeated, his courage is already broken—who knows whether he can in the end devote himself fully to Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when Ning hears Yanzhang's army was defeated, his courage is already broken. Who knows whether he can in the end devote himself fully to Your Majesty!

sentences.zh: 趙巖曰：「事勢如此，一下此樓，誰心可保！」

translations.literal: Zhao Yan said, "The situation being thus, once you descend this tower, who can guarantee his heart!
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yan said, "The situation being thus, once you descend this tower, who can guarantee anyone's loyalty!

sentences.zh: 梁主乃止。

translations.literal: The Liang emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor then stopped.

sentences.zh: 復召宰相謀之，鄭玨請自懷傳國寶詐降以紓國難，梁主曰：「今日固不敢愛寶，但如卿此策，竟可了否？」

translations.literal: He again summoned the grand councilors to consult; Zheng Jue asked to carry the imperial seal under his robe and feign surrender to ease the national crisis; the Liang emperor said, "Today I truly dare not begrudge the seal—but with your plan as this, can it really settle matters?
translations.idiomatic: He again summoned the grand councilors to consult. Zheng Jue asked to carry the imperial seal under his robe and feign surrender to ease the national crisis. The Liang emperor said, "Today I truly dare not begrudge the seal—but with your plan as this, can it really settle matters?

sentences.zh: 玨俯首久之，曰：「但恐未了。」

translations.literal: Jue bowed his head a long time and said, "I fear only that it cannot settle them.
translations.idiomatic: Jue bowed his head a long time and said, "I fear only that it cannot settle them.

sentences.zh: 左右皆縮頸而笑。

translations.literal: Those nearby all shrank their necks and laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Those nearby all shrank their necks and laughed.

sentences.zh: 梁主日夜涕泣，不知所為；

translations.literal: Day and night the Liang emperor wept tears, not knowing what to do;
translations.idiomatic: Day and night the Liang emperor wept, not knowing what to do;

sentences.zh: 置傳國寶於臥內，忽失之，已為左右竊之迎唐軍矣。

translations.literal: He placed the imperial seal inside his bedchamber; suddenly it was lost—it had already been stolen by attendants to welcome the Tang army.
translations.idiomatic: He placed the imperial seal inside his bedchamber, and suddenly it was lost—it had already been stolen by attendants to welcome the Tang army.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，或告唐軍已過曹州，塵埃漲天，趙巖謂從者曰：「吾待溫許州厚，必不負我。」

translations.literal: On wuyin someone reported Tang troops had already passed Cao Prefecture—dust filled the sky; Zhao Yan said to those with him, "I treated Wen of Xuzhou generously—he will surely not fail me.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin someone reported Tang troops had already passed Cao Prefecture—dust filled the sky. Zhao Yan said to those with him, "I treated Wen of Xuzhou generously—he will surely not fail me.

sentences.zh: 遂奔許州。

translations.literal: Then he fled to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Then he fled to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 梁主謂皇甫麟曰：「李氏吾世仇，理難降首，不可俟彼刀鋸。

translations.literal: The Liang emperor said to Huangfu Lin, "The Li clan are my hereditary enemies; by rights I cannot bow my head in surrender—I cannot wait for their blades and saws.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor said to Huangfu Lin, "The Li clan are my hereditary enemies; by rights I cannot bow my head in surrender. I cannot wait for their blades and saws.

sentences.zh: 吾不能自裁，卿可斷吾首。」

translations.literal: I cannot kill myself—you may cut off my head.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot kill myself—you may cut off my head.

sentences.zh: 麟泣曰：「臣為陛下揮劍死唐軍則可矣，不敢奉此詔。」

translations.literal: Lin wept and said, "Your subject can die swinging his sword against Tang troops, but I dare not obey this edict.
translations.idiomatic: Lin wept and said, "Your subject can die swinging his sword against Tang troops, but I dare not obey this edict.

sentences.zh: 梁主曰：「卿欲賣我邪？」

translations.literal: The Liang emperor said, "Do you wish to sell me out?
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor said, "Do you wish to sell me out?

sentences.zh: 麟欲自剄，梁主持之曰：「與卿俱死！」

translations.literal: Lin wished to cut his own throat; the Liang emperor held him and said, "Let us die together!
translations.idiomatic: Lin wished to cut his own throat; the Liang emperor held him and said, "Let us die together!

sentences.zh: 麟遂弒梁主，因自殺。

translations.literal: Lin then killed the Liang emperor and took his own life.
translations.idiomatic: Lin then killed the Liang emperor and took his own life.

sentences.zh: 梁主為人溫恭儉約，無荒淫之失；

translations.literal: The Liang emperor as a man was mild, respectful, and frugal—there was no excess of licentiousness;
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor as a man was mild, respectful, and frugal—there was no excess of licentiousness;

sentences.zh: 但寵信趙、張，使擅威福，疏棄敬、李舊臣，不用其言，以至於亡。

translations.literal: But he favored and trusted Zhao and Zhang, letting them wield power and privilege at will; he estranged and cast aside old ministers Jing and Li and did not use their counsel—thus he came to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: But he favored and trusted Zhao and Zhang, letting them wield power and privilege at will. He estranged and cast aside old ministers Jing and Li and did not use their counsel, and thus he came to ruin.

sentences.zh: 己卯旦，李嗣源軍至大梁，攻封丘門，王瓚開門出降，嗣源入城，撫安軍民。

translations.literal: At dawn on jimao Li Siyuan's army reached Daliang and attacked Fengqiu Gate; Wang Zan opened the gate and came out to surrender; Siyuan entered the city and pacified troops and people.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on jimao Li Siyuan's army reached Daliang and attacked Fengqiu Gate. Wang Zan opened the gate and came out to surrender. Siyuan entered the city and pacified troops and people.

sentences.zh: 是日，帝入自梁門，百官迎謁於馬首，拜伏請罪，帝慰勞之，使各復其位。

translations.literal: That day the emperor entered through Liang Gate; the hundred officials welcomed and paid obeisance at his horse's head, prostrating themselves to beg forgiveness; the emperor comforted them and had each resume his post.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor entered through Liang Gate. The hundred officials welcomed and paid obeisance at his horse's head, prostrating themselves to beg forgiveness. The emperor comforted them and had each resume his post.

sentences.zh: 李嗣源迎賀，帝喜不自勝，手引嗣源衣，以頭觸之曰：「吾有天下，卿父子之功也，天下與爾共之。」

translations.literal: Li Siyuan came to welcome and congratulate; the emperor was beyond himself with joy; he took Siyuan's robe in hand and touched his head to it, saying, "I have the realm—this is the achievement of you father and son; the realm I share with you.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siyuan came to welcome and congratulate. The emperor was beyond himself with joy. He took Siyuan's robe in hand and touched his head to it, saying, "I have the realm—this is the achievement of you father and son. The realm I share with you.

sentences.zh: 帝命訪求梁主，頃之，或以其首獻。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered a search for the Liang emperor; before long someone presented his head.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered a search for the Liang emperor, and before long someone presented his head.

sentences.zh: 李振謂敬翔曰：「有詔洗滌吾輩，相與朝新君乎？」

translations.literal: Li Zhen said to Jing Xiang, "There is an edict to wash us clean—shall we together attend the new sovereign at court?
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhen said to Jing Xiang, "There is an edict to wash us clean—shall we together attend the new sovereign at court?

sentences.zh: 翔曰：「吾二人為梁宰相，君昏不能諫，國亡不能救，新君若問，將何辭以對！」

translations.literal: Xiang said, "We two were Liang grand councilors; the ruler was benighted and we could not remonstrate; the state perished and we could not save it; if the new sovereign asks, with what words shall we answer!
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said, "We two were Liang grand councilors. The ruler was benighted and we could not remonstrate; the state perished and we could not save it. If the new sovereign asks, with what words shall we answer!

sentences.zh: 是夕未曙，或報翔曰：「崇政李太保已入朝矣。」

translations.literal: That evening before daybreak someone reported to Xiang, "Guard of the Inner Palace Li the Grand Protector has already entered court.
translations.idiomatic: That evening before daybreak someone reported to Xiang, "Guard of the Inner Palace Li the Grand Protector has already entered court.

sentences.zh: 翔歎曰：「李振謬為丈夫！

translations.literal: Xiang sighed and said, "Li Zhen wrongly poses as a man of honor!
translations.idiomatic: Xiang sighed and said, "Li Zhen wrongly poses as a man of honor!

sentences.zh: 朱氏與新君世為仇讎，今國亡君死，縱新君不誅，何面目入建國門乎！」

translations.literal: Lady Zhu and the new ruler have been mortal enemies for generations; now the state is destroyed and the lord dead—even if the new ruler does not execute me, with what face could I enter Jianguo Gate!
translations.idiomatic: The Zhu clan and the new emperor had been sworn enemies for generations. Now the state was lost and its ruler dead. Even if the new emperor spared my life, how could I bear to walk through Jianguo Gate again?

sentences.zh: 乃縊而死。

translations.literal: She then hanged herself and died.
translations.idiomatic: With that she hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，梁百官復待罪於朝堂，帝宣敕赦之。

translations.literal: On gengchen, the Liang hundred officials again awaited punishment in the court hall; the emperor proclaimed an edict pardoning them.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen the Liang officials once more stood in the hall awaiting judgment. The emperor issued an edict of pardon.

sentences.zh: 趙巖至許州，溫昭圖迎謁歸第，斬首來獻，盡沒巖所繼之貨。

translations.literal: Zhao Yan reached Xuzhou; Wen Zhaotu welcomed him in audience, escorted him to his residence, beheaded him and presented the head, and confiscated all goods Yan had inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Yan arrived at Xuzhou, Wen Zhaotu received him with ceremony, brought him home, cut off his head and sent it in tribute, and seized every item of property Yan had come into.

sentences.zh: 昭圖復名韜。

translations.literal: Zhaotu resumed the name Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaotu took back his original name, Tao.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，詔王瓚收朱友貞屍，殯於佛寺，漆其首，函之，藏於太社。

translations.literal: On xinsi, an edict ordered Wang Zan to recover Zhu Youzhen's corpse, lay it out in a Buddhist temple, lacquer the head, place it in a casket, and store it at the Imperial Altar of Earth.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi the emperor ordered Wang Zan to recover Zhu Youzhen's body, lay it out in a Buddhist temple, lacquer the severed head, seal it in a box, and deposit it at the Imperial Altar of Earth.

sentences.zh: 段凝自滑州濟河入援，以諸軍排陳使杜晏球為前鋒；

translations.literal: Duan Ning crossed the river from Huazhou to enter as relief, making Du Yanqiu, commissioner for array formation of the various armies, vanguard;
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ning crossed the Yellow River from Huazhou to bring reinforcements, appointing Du Yanqiu, commissioner for battle formation among the combined forces, as vanguard;

sentences.zh: 至封丘，遇李從珂，晏球先降。

translations.literal: Reaching Fengqiu they encountered Li Congke; Yanqiu surrendered first.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengqiu they ran into Li Congke, and Yanqiu was the first to submit.

sentences.zh: 壬午，凝將其眾五萬至封丘，亦解甲請降。

translations.literal: On renwu, Ning brought his host of fifty thousand to Fengqiu and likewise removed armor to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Ning marched his fifty thousand men to Fengqiu and, like Yanqiu, laid down their arms and offered surrender.

sentences.zh: 凝帥諸大將先詣闕待罪，帝勞賜之，慰諭士卒，使各復其所。

translations.literal: Ning led the great generals to first go to the palace to await punishment; the emperor rewarded and comforted them, reassured the soldiers, and had each return to his place.
translations.idiomatic: Ning led his senior commanders to the palace to await judgment. The emperor received them with rewards and kind words, reassured the rank and file, and sent everyone back to his post.

sentences.zh: 凝出入公卿間，揚揚自得無愧色，梁之舊臣見者皆欲齕其面，抉其心。

translations.literal: Ning moved among the high ministers, high-spirited and self-satisfied without a shade of shame; Liang old ministers who saw him all wanted to bite his face and gouge out his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Ning walked among the court grandees with an easy, unashamed air. Every former Liang minister who saw him wished he could tear off his face and rip out his heart.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，詔貶梁中書侍郎、同平章事鄭玨為萊州司戶，蕭頃為登州司戶，翰林學士劉岳為均州司馬，任贊為房州司馬，姚顗為復州司馬，封翹為唐州司馬，李懌為懷州司馬，竇夢征為沂州司馬，崇政學士劉光素為密州司戶，陸崇為安州司戶，御史中丞王權為隨州司戶；

translations.literal: On bingxu, an edict demoted Zheng Jue, Liang Vice Chancellor of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor, to Laizhou census clerk; Xiao Xiang to Dengzhou census clerk; Hanlin academician Liu Yue to Junzhou assistant prefect; Ren Zan to Fangzhou assistant prefect; Yao Yi to Fuzhou assistant prefect; Feng Qiao to Tangzhou assistant prefect; Li Yi to Huaizhou assistant prefect; Dou Mengzheng to Yizhou assistant prefect; Chongzheng academician Liu Guangsu to Mizhou census clerk; Lu Chong to Anzhou census clerk; and Censor-in-Chief Wang Quan to Suizhou census clerk;
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu an edict stripped rank from a slate of Liang grandees who had risen high under the old regime: Zheng Jue, Vice Chancellor of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor, was reduced to census clerk of Laizhou; Xiao Xiang to Dengzhou; Liu Yue, Hanlin academician, to Junzhou; Ren Zan to Fangzhou; Yao Yi to Fuzhou; Feng Qiao to Tangzhou; Li Yi to Huaizhou; Dou Mengzheng to Yizhou; Liu Guangsu, Chongzheng academician, to Mizhou; Lu Chong to Anzhou; and Wang Quan, Censor-in-Chief, to Suizhou—all as assistant prefects or census clerks;

sentences.zh: 以其世受唐恩而仕梁貴顯故也。

translations.literal: This was because they had received Tang grace for generations yet served Liang in exalted rank.
translations.idiomatic: The reason was that their families had owed the Tang dynasty generations of favor, yet they had taken high office under Liang.

sentences.zh: 岳，崇龜之從子；

translations.literal: Yue was the nephew of Chonggui;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yue was a nephew of Liu Chonggui;

sentences.zh: 顗，萬年人；

translations.literal: Yi was a man of Wannian;
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yi came from Wannian;

sentences.zh: 翹，敖之孫；

translations.literal: Qiao was the grandson of Ao;
translations.idiomatic: Feng Qiao was a grandson of Feng Ao;

sentences.zh: 懌，亦兆人；

translations.literal: Yi was also a man of Jingzhao;
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi was likewise a native of the capital district;

sentences.zh: 權，龜之孫也。

translations.literal: Quan was the grandson of Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Quan was a grandson of Wang Gui.

sentences.zh: 段凝、杜晏球上言：「偽梁要人趙巖、趙鵠、張希逸、張漢倫、張漢傑、張漢融、朱珪等，竊弄威福，殘蠹群生，不可不誅。」

translations.literal: Duan Ning and Du Yanqiu submitted a memorial: "The false Liang power-holders Zhao Yan, Zhao Hu, Zhang Xiyi, Zhang Hanlun, Zhang Hanjie, Zhang Hanrong, Zhu Gui, and others secretly wielded authority and favor, ravaging and harming the people—they cannot go unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ning and Du Yanqiu memorialized the throne: "Among the leading men of the usurper Liang—Zhao Yan, Zhao Hu, Zhang Xiyi, Zhang Hanlun, Zhang Hanjie, Zhang Hanrong, Zhu Gui, and the rest—many abused their power to prey on the realm. They must be put to death."

sentences.zh: 詔：「敬翔、李振首佐朱溫，共傾唐祚；

translations.literal: An edict: "Jing Xiang and Li Zhen first assisted Zhu Wen in jointly overturning the Tang mandate;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor responded with an edict: "Jing Xiang and Li Zhen were the first to aid Zhu Wen in bringing down the Tang;

sentences.zh: 契丹撒刺阿撥叛兄棄母，負恩背國，宜與巖等並族誅於市；

translations.literal: the Khitan Salagabo rebelled against his elder brother and abandoned his mother, betraying grace and country—they should together with Yan and the others be executed by clan extermination in the marketplace;
translations.idiomatic: the Khitan Salagabo rebelled against his brother and forsook his mother, ingratitude and treason together—they, together with Yan and his associates, shall be executed in the market and their clans extirpated;

sentences.zh: 自餘文武將吏一切不問。」

translations.literal: as for the remaining civil and military officers and clerks, none shall be questioned.
translations.idiomatic: All other civil and military officers and clerks shall be left unmolested."

sentences.zh: 又詔追廢朱溫、朱友貞為庶人，毀其宗廟神主。

translations.literal: Another edict posthumously deposed Zhu Wen and Zhu Youzhen as commoners and destroyed their ancestral temple spirit tablets.
translations.idiomatic: A further edict posthumously reduced Zhu Wen and Zhu Youzhen to commoners and demolished the spirit tablets in their ancestral shrine.

sentences.zh: 帝之與梁戰於河上也，梁拱宸左廂都指揮使陸思鐸善射，常於笴上自鏤姓名，射帝，中馬鞍，帝拔箭藏之。

translations.literal: When the emperor fought Liang on the river, Lu Siduo, commander of the left wing of the Gongchen guard, was skilled at archery; he often carved his name on his arrows, shot at the emperor, struck the saddle, and the emperor pulled out the arrow and hid it.
translations.idiomatic: During the fighting on the river against Liang, Lu Siduo of the Gongchen guard's left wing was a crack archer who engraved his name on every shaft. He once shot at the emperor and hit the saddle. The emperor quietly pulled out the arrow and kept it hidden.

sentences.zh: 至是，思鐸從眾俱降，帝出箭示之，思鐸伏地待罪，帝慰而釋之，尋授龍武右廂都指揮使。

translations.literal: At this time Siduo surrendered with the rest; the emperor produced the arrow and showed it to him; Siduo prostrated himself to await punishment; the emperor comforted and released him, and soon appointed him commander of the right wing of the Longwu guard.
translations.idiomatic: Now Siduo surrendered with his men. The emperor brought out the arrow and showed it to him. Siduo fell prostrate to await judgment, but the emperor reassured him and let him go, soon naming him commander of the Longwu guard's right wing.

sentences.zh: 以豆盧革尚在魏，命樞密使郭崇韜權行中書事。

translations.literal: Because Doulu Ge was still in Wei, the emperor ordered Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner Guo Chongtao to act concurrently in chancellery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: With Doulu Ge still at Weizhou, the emperor had Guo Chongtao, commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, serve temporarily as acting head of the chancellery.

sentences.zh: 梁諸籓鎮稍稍入朝，或上表待罪，帝皆慰釋之。

translations.literal: The various Liang military commissions gradually entered court, some submitting memorials to await punishment; the emperor in every case comforted and released them.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's regional commanders began trickling in to court, some sending memorials begging forgiveness. The emperor received them all with reassurance and pardon.

sentences.zh: 宋州節度使袁象先首來入朝，陝州留後霍彥威次之。

translations.literal: Yuan Xiangxian, military commissioner of Songzhou, was first to come to court; Huo Yanwei, acting commissioner of Shanzhou, came next.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiangxian of Songzhou was the first to arrive; Huo Yanwei, acting commissioner of Shanzhou, followed.

sentences.zh: 像先輦珍貨數十萬，遍賂劉夫人及權貴、伶官、宦者，旬日，中外爭譽之，恩寵隆異。

translations.literal: Xiangxian conveyed treasures worth several hundred thousand, bribing Lady Liu and the powerful, actors, and eunuchs throughout; within ten days inner and outer court alike competed in praising him, and favor and grace were lofty and extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangxian sent in treasures worth hundreds of thousands and spread gifts among Lady Liu, the great officers, actors, and eunuchs. Within ten days the whole court was praising him, and imperial favor fell on him in unusual measure.

sentences.zh: 己丑，詔偽庭節度、觀察、防禦、團練使、刺史及諸將校，並不議改更，將校官吏先奔偽庭者一切不問。

translations.literal: On jichou, an edict: the usurper court's military commissioners, observation commissioners, defense commissioners, training commissioners, prefects, and all generals and officers—none shall be discussed for replacement; generals, officers, and clerks who had earlier fled to the usurper court shall none be questioned.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou an edict declared that every military commissioner, observation commissioner, defense commissioner, training commissioner, prefect, and field officer appointed by the usurper regime would keep his post without review, and that no one who had earlier gone over to Liang would be called to account.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，豆盧革至自魏。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Doulu Ge arrived from Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Doulu Ge returned from Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 甲午，加崇韜守侍中，領成德節度使。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Chongtao was further made acting Palace Attendant and given charge of the Chengde military commission.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Guo Chongtao was promoted to acting Palace Attendant and appointed military commissioner of Chengde.

sentences.zh: 崇韜權兼內外，謀猷規益，竭忠無隱，頗亦薦引人物，豆盧革受成而已，無所裁正。

translations.literal: Chongtao wielded authority over both inner and outer affairs; in counsel and planning he was wholly loyal without concealment, and also frequently recommended men; Doulu Ge simply accepted what was settled and had nothing to revise or correct.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao held real power over court and camp alike. He gave frank, loyal counsel and brought forward capable men. Doulu Ge, by contrast, merely ratified decisions already made and exercised no independent judgment.

sentences.zh: 丙申，賜滑州留後段凝姓名曰李紹欽，耀州刺史杜晏球曰李紹虔。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Duan Ning, acting commissioner of Huazhou, was granted the surname and personal name Li Shaoqin; Du Yanqiu, prefect of Yaozhou, was granted Li Shaoqian.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen the emperor bestowed the Tang surname Li and the name Shaoqin on Duan Ning, acting commissioner of Huazhou, and the name Shaoqian on Du Yanqiu, prefect of Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，梁西都留守河南尹張宗奭來朝，復名全義，獻幣馬千計；

translations.literal: On yiyou, Zhang Zongshi, western-capital garrison commander and Henan governor, came to court, resumed the name Quanyi, and presented gifts of silk and horses numbering in the thousands;
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou Zhang Zongshi, Liang's western-capital garrison commander and governor of Henan, arrived at court, restored his former name Quanyi, and offered thousands of horses and bolts of tribute silk;

sentences.zh: 帝命皇子繼岌、皇弟存紀等兄事之。

translations.literal: the emperor ordered the crown prince Jiji, the imperial younger brother Cunji, and others to treat him as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor commanded his son Li Jiji, his younger brother Li Cunji, and the other princes to honor him as an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 帝欲發梁太祖墓，斫棺焚其屍，全義上言：「朱溫雖國之深仇，然其人已死，刑無可加，屠滅其家，足以為報，乞免焚斫以存聖恩。」

translations.literal: The emperor wished to open the tomb of the Liang Founding Emperor, split the coffin, and burn the corpse; Quanyi submitted a memorial: "Although Zhu Wen was the state's deep enemy, the man is already dead and punishment can go no further; exterminating his house is sufficient as revenge—I beg that burning and splitting be waived to preserve sagely grace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to open the Liang Founding Emperor's tomb, break the coffin, and burn the body. Quanyi pleaded: "Zhu Wen was indeed the dynasty's bitter foe, but he is dead and beyond further punishment. His house has already been destroyed—that is revenge enough. I beg Your Majesty to forgo desecration of the grave and show magnanimity."

sentences.zh: 帝從之，但鏟其闕室，削封樹而已。

translations.literal: The emperor assented, only scraping away the tomb chamber and cutting back the planted trees.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, contenting himself with stripping the tomb mound and trimming the memorial trees.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，加天平節度使李嗣源兼中書令；

translations.literal: On wuxu, Li Siyuan, military commissioner of Tianping, was further made concurrent Director of the Chancellery;
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Li Siyuan, military commissioner of Tianping, was also named Director of the Chancellery;

sentences.zh: 以北京留守繼岌為東京留守、同平章事。

translations.literal: the northern-capital garrison commander Jiji was made eastern-capital garrison commander and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiji, garrison commander of the northern capital, was appointed garrison commander of the eastern capital and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使宣諭諸道，梁所除節度使五十餘人皆上表入貢。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched envoys to announce and instruct the various circuits; more than fifty military commissioners appointed by Liang all submitted memorials and sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys throughout the realm with proclamations of the new order. More than fifty military commissioners Liang had appointed all memorialized the throne and sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 楚王殷遣其子牙內馬步都指揮使希范入見，納洪、鄂行營都統印，上本道將吏籍。

translations.literal: King Yin of Chu sent his son Xi Fan, commander of palace inner horse and foot, to audience, surrendering the seals of overall commander of the Hong and E field headquarters and submitting the register of this circuit's generals and clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yin of Chu sent his son Xi Fan, commander of the palace guard, to court. Xi Fan surrendered the seals of the Hong-E field command and submitted a full roster of Chu officers and officials.

sentences.zh: 荊南節度使高季昌聞帝滅梁，避唐廟諱，更名季興，欲自入朝，梁震曰：「唐有吞天下之志，嚴兵守險，猶恐不自保，況數千里入朝乎！

translations.literal: Gao Jichang, military commissioner of Jingnan, hearing the emperor had destroyed Liang, avoided the Tang temple taboo and changed his name to Jixing; he wished to go to court in person; Liang Zhen said: "Tang has the ambition to swallow the realm; with strict troops guarding the passes it still fears it cannot preserve itself—how much less travel several thousand li to court!
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Jichang of Jingnan learned that Tang had overthrown Liang, he changed his name to Jixing to avoid a taboo character and prepared to go to court himself. His adviser Liang Zhen warned: "Tang means to swallow the whole realm. Even with strong garrisons on every pass they may not feel secure—what hope is there in traveling thousands of li to pay homage?

sentences.zh: 且公朱氏舊將，安知彼不以仇敵相遇乎！」

translations.literal: Moreover, my lord, you are an old general of the Zhu clan—how can you know they will not meet you as an enemy!
translations.idiomatic: And you, sir, were once a general of the Zhu house. Who is to say they will not receive you as an enemy?"

sentences.zh: 季興不從。

translations.literal: Jixing did not follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Jixing would not listen.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使以滅梁告吳、蜀，二國皆懼。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched envoys to announce the destruction of Liang to Wu and Shu; both states were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to Wu and Shu with news of Liang's fall. Both courts were alarmed.

sentences.zh: 徐溫尤嚴可求曰：「公前沮吾計，今將奈何？」

translations.literal: Xu Wen was especially stern with Yan Keqiu, saying: "You formerly blocked my plan—what now shall we do?
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen turned on Yan Keqiu with unusual severity: "You talked me out of my plan before. What do you propose we do now?

sentences.zh: 可求笑曰：「聞唐主始得中原，志氣驕滿，御下無法，不出數年，將有內變，吾但當卑辭厚禮，保境安民以待之耳。」

translations.literal: Keqiu smiled and said: "I hear the Tang ruler has just gained the central plains, his spirit proud and full, governing subordinates without method—in no more than a few years there will be internal turmoil; we need only use humble words and rich gifts, secure the borders and settle the people, and wait.
translations.idiomatic: Keqiu smiled and replied: "They say the Tang emperor has just taken the heartland, swollen with pride and loose in discipline. Give him a few years and there will be trouble within. Our task is to speak humbly, send rich gifts, hold our borders, and keep the people at peace until that day comes."

sentences.zh: 唐使稱詔，吳人不受；

translations.literal: The Tang envoy styled his message an imperial edict; the Wu people did not accept it;
translations.idiomatic: The Tang envoy presented his letter as an imperial edict, and Wu refused to receive it;

sentences.zh: 帝易其書，用敵國之禮，曰：「大唐皇帝致書於吳國主」，吳人復書稱「大吳國主上大唐皇帝」，辭禮如箋表。

translations.literal: the emperor changed the letter, using the protocol of equal states: "The Great Tang emperor sends a letter to the Wu state lord"; the Wu people replied addressing "the Great Wu state lord to the Great Tang emperor," wording and ritual like a formal memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor revised the text to treat Wu as an equal power: "The emperor of Great Tang to the lord of Wu." Wu answered in kind—"The lord of Great Wu to the emperor of Great Tang"—in the form of a formal memorial between sovereigns.

sentences.zh: 吳人有告壽州團練使鍾泰章侵市官馬者，徐知誥以吳王之命，遣滁州刺史王稔巡霍丘，因代為壽州團練使，以泰章為饒州刺史。

translations.literal: A Wu man reported that Zhong Taizhang, training commissioner of Shouzhou, had seized and sold government horses; Xu Zhigao, by the Wu king's order, sent Wang Min, prefect of Chuzhou, to inspect Huoqiu, and thereby replaced him as Shouzhou training commissioner, making Taizhang prefect of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Someone in Wu accused Zhong Taizhang, training commissioner of Shouzhou, of seizing and selling government horses. Acting on the Wu king's orders, Xu Zhigao sent Wang Min, prefect of Chuzhou, to inspect Huoqiu, took Shouzhou from Taizhang, and transferred him to Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 徐溫召至金陵，使陳彥謙詰之者三，皆不對。

translations.literal: Xu Wen summoned him to Jinling and had Chen Yanqian question him three times; he answered nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen had him brought to Jinling and ordered Chen Yanqian to interrogate him three times. Taizhang refused to reply.

sentences.zh: 或問泰章：「可以不自辨？」

translations.literal: Someone asked Taizhang: "Can you not defend yourself?
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked Taizhang: "Will you not speak in your own defense?

sentences.zh: 泰章曰：「吾在揚州，十萬軍中號稱壯士；

translations.literal: Taizhang said: "When I was at Yangzhou, among a hundred thousand troops I was called a stalwart;
translations.idiomatic: Taizhang answered: "At Yangzhou I was known as the bravest man in an army of a hundred thousand;

sentences.zh: 壽州去淮數里，步騎不下五千，苟有它志，豈王稔單騎能代之乎！

translations.literal: Shouzhou is several li from the Huai, with no fewer than five thousand infantry and cavalry—if I had other designs, how could Wang Min alone on a single horse replace me!
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhou lies only a few li from the Huai, with five thousand foot and horse under my command. If I had meant rebellion, could Wang Min have replaced me single-handed on one horse?

sentences.zh: 我義不負國，雖黜為縣令亦行，況刺史乎！

translations.literal: My righteousness does not fail the state—even demoted to county magistrate I would go, how much more as prefect!
translations.idiomatic: My loyalty to the state is clear. I would accept even demotion to county magistrate—how much less object to a prefecture!

sentences.zh: 何為自辨以彰朝廷之失！」

translations.literal: Why should I defend myself and thereby expose the court's error!
translations.idiomatic: Why should I argue my case and advertise the court's mistake?"

sentences.zh: 徐知誥欲以法繩諸將，請收泰章治罪。

translations.literal: Xu Zhigao wished to bind the generals by law and requested that Taizhang be taken and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhigao wanted to make an example under the law and asked that Taizhang be arrested and prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 徐溫曰：「吾非泰章，已死於張顥之手，今日富貴，安可負之！」

translations.literal: Xu Wen said: "Had it not been for Taizhang, I would already have died at Zhang Hao's hands—today's wealth and honor, how could I fail him!
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen said: "If not for Taizhang I would have died at Zhang Hao's hands. With the wealth and rank I enjoy today, how could I turn against him?

sentences.zh: 命知誥為子景通娶其女以解之。

translations.literal: He ordered Zhigao to have his son Jingtong marry Taizhang's daughter to resolve the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He settled the affair by arranging for Zhigao's son Jingtong to marry Taizhang's daughter.

sentences.zh: 彗星見輿鬼，長丈餘，蜀司天監言國有大災。

translations.literal: A comet appeared in the Yue-Gui asterism, more than a zhang in length; the Shu Directorate of Astronomy said the state would suffer great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: A comet more than ten feet long appeared in the Yue-Gui asterism. The Shu Directorate of Astronomy declared that the realm faced a great disaster.

sentences.zh: 蜀主詔於玉局化設道場，右補闕張雲上疏，以為：「百姓怨氣上徹於天，故彗星見。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler ordered a ritual arena established at Yujuhua; Right Remonstrance Zhang Yun submitted a memorial, holding: "The people's resentful qi rises to penetrate heaven—therefore the comet appears.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu emperor ordered rites performed at Yujuhua. Right Remonstrance Zhang Yun memorialized the throne: "The people's grievances have risen to heaven—that is why the comet has appeared.

sentences.zh: 此乃亡國之征，非祈禳可弭。」

translations.literal: This is a sign of a state's destruction—not something prayer and exorcism can dispel.
translations.idiomatic: It is an omen of dynastic fall, not an evil that ritual prayer can avert."

sentences.zh: 蜀主怒，流雲黎州，卒於道。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler was angry, exiled Yun to Lizhou, and he died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu emperor in a rage banished Zhang Yun to Lizhou. He died on the way.

sentences.zh: 郭崇韜上言：「河南節度使、刺史上表者但稱姓名，未除新官，恐負憂疑。」

translations.literal: Guo Chongtao submitted a memorial: "The Henan military commissioners and prefects who submit memorials only give their names; new offices have not been conferred—I fear this will breed worry and doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao wrote: "Henan's military commissioners and prefects are memorializing under their old names because no new appointments have been issued. That is bound to leave them anxious and uncertain."

sentences.zh: 十一月，始降制以新官命之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, edicts were at last issued appointing them to new offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the emperor finally issued formal appointments under the new regime.

sentences.zh: 滑州留後李紹欽因伶人景進納貨於宮掖，除泰寧節度使。

translations.literal: Li Shaoqin, acting commissioner of Huazhou, through the actor Jing Jin presented goods within the palace precincts and was appointed military commissioner of Taining.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaoqin, acting commissioner of Huazhou, secured the post of military commissioner of Taining by bribing the palace through the actor Jing Jin.

sentences.zh: 帝幼善音律，故伶人多有寵，常侍左右；

translations.literal: The emperor from youth was skilled in music, so actors often enjoyed favor and constantly attended at his side;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had loved music since boyhood, and actors accordingly enjoyed great favor, always at his side;

sentences.zh: 帝或時自傅粉墨，與優人共戲於庭，以悅劉夫人，優名謂之「李天下！」

translations.literal: The emperor sometimes applied his own greasepaint, playing in the courtyard with performers to please Lady Liu; the performers called him by the name "Li Tianxia!"
translations.idiomatic: He sometimes painted his own face and played scenes in the courtyard with the troupe to amuse Lady Liu. Onstage they hailed him as "Li Tianxia!"—"Li Who Rules the Realm!"

sentences.zh: 嘗因為優，自呼曰：「李天下，李天下」，優人敬新磨遽前批其頰。

translations.literal: Once while acting as a performer he called himself "Li Tianxia, Li Tianxia"; the performer Jing Xinmo swiftly stepped forward and slapped his cheek.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while playing a part, he cried out, "Li Tianxia! Li Tianxia!" The actor Jing Xinmo darted forward and struck him across the face.

sentences.zh: 帝失色，群優亦駭愕，新磨徐曰：「理天下者只有一人，尚誰呼邪！」

translations.literal: The emperor changed color; the troupe of performers were also startled; Xinmo slowly said: "He who orders the realm is only one person—whom else are you calling!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went pale and the whole troupe froze in terror. Xinmo said calmly: "Only one man may rule the realm—whom else do you mean to summon?

sentences.zh: 帝悅，厚賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and richly rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and gave him a generous reward.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗畋於中牟，踐民稼，中牟令當馬前諫曰：「陛下為民父母，奈何毀其所食，使轉死溝壑乎！」

translations.literal: The emperor once hunted at Zhongmou, trampling the people's crops; the Zhongmou magistrate blocked his horse and remonstrated: "Your Majesty is parent to the people—how can you destroy what they eat and make them die turning in ditches and gullies!
translations.idiomatic: On a hunt at Zhongmou the emperor rode through standing grain. The county magistrate stepped in front of his horse and pleaded: "Your Majesty is father and mother to the people. Why trample their food and drive them to starve in the ditches?

sentences.zh: 帝怒，叱去，將殺之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, shouted him away, and was about to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, ordered him driven off, and was ready to execute him.

sentences.zh: 敬新磨追擒至馬前，責之曰：「汝為縣令，獨不知吾天子好獵邪？

translations.literal: Jing Xinmo pursued, seized him, and brought him before the horse, reproaching him: "You are a county magistrate—do you alone not know our Son of Heaven loves the hunt?
translations.idiomatic: Jing Xinmo ran after him, dragged him back to the horse, and scolded him: "You are a county magistrate—do you alone not know that our emperor loves to hunt?

sentences.zh: 奈何縱民耕種，以妨吾天子之馳聘乎！

translations.literal: How dare you let the people plow and sow, obstructing our Son of Heaven's galloping!
translations.idiomatic: Why did you let peasants plant crops and block our emperor's riding ground!

sentences.zh: 汝罪當死！」

translations.literal: Your crime deserves death!
translations.idiomatic: You deserve to die for this!

sentences.zh: 因請行刑，帝笑而釋之。

translations.literal: He then requested to carry out the execution; the emperor laughed and released the magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He asked leave to carry out the sentence on the spot. The emperor laughed and let the magistrate go.

sentences.zh: 諸伶出入宮掖，侮弄縉紳，群臣憤嫉，莫敢出氣；

translations.literal: The various actors came and went within the palace precincts, mocking and playing with the gentry-robed; the hundred ministers were angry and resentful but dared not breathe a word;
translations.idiomatic: Actors moved freely in and out of the inner palace, humiliating court gentlemen. Ministers seethed with anger but none dared speak;

sentences.zh: 亦反有相附托以希恩澤者，四方籓鎮爭以貨賂結之。

translations.literal: there were also those who instead attached themselves in reliance, hoping for grace and favor; the regional commands on all sides competed in bribing them with goods.
translations.idiomatic: some officials instead cultivated them for favor, and regional commanders across the realm vied to buy their goodwill with gifts.

sentences.zh: 其尤蠹政害人者，景進為之首。

translations.literal: Of those who most harmed government and harmed people, Jing Jin was chief.
translations.idiomatic: The worst of them, the one who most poisoned government, was Jing Jin.

sentences.zh: 進好采閭閻鄙細事聞於上，上亦欲知外間事，遂委進以耳目。

translations.literal: Jin liked to gather petty affairs from lanes and alleys to report to the ruler; the ruler also wished to know outside affairs, and therefore entrusted Jin as eyes and ears.
translations.idiomatic: Jin delighted in collecting trivial gossip from the streets and reporting it upstairs. The emperor, eager for news from beyond the palace, made him his informant.

sentences.zh: 進每奏事，常屏左右問之，由是進得施其讒慝，干預政事。

translations.literal: Whenever Jin reported affairs he usually dismissed attendants to question privately; thereby Jin was able to deploy slander and malice and intervene in government.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Jin came to report, he would send attendants away for a private audience. In this way he spread slander and meddled in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 自將相大臣皆憚之，孔巖常以兄事之。

translations.literal: From generals and chancellors to great ministers all feared him; Kong Yan often treated him as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Even generals and grand councilors stood in awe of him. Kong Yan regularly addressed him as an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，岐王遣使致書，賀帝滅梁，以季父自居，辭禮甚倨。

translations.literal: On renyin, the Prince of Qi sent envoys with a letter congratulating the emperor on destroying Liang, placing himself as paternal uncle, with wording and ritual very arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin the Prince of Qi sent a letter congratulating the emperor on the fall of Liang. He styled himself the emperor's uncle-by-marriage and wrote in a tone of open arrogance.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，河中節度使朱友謙入朝，帝與之宴，寵錫無算。

translations.literal: On guimao, Zhu Youqian, military commissioner of Hezhong, entered court; the emperor feasted with him and bestowed favor beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Zhu Youqian of Hezhong came to court. The emperor held a banquet in his honor and showered him with rewards beyond number.

sentences.zh: 張全義請帝遷都洛陽，從之。

translations.literal: Zhang Quanyi requested the emperor move the capital to Luoyang; the emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quanyi urged the emperor to transfer the capital to Luoyang, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 己巳，賜朱友謙姓名曰李繼麟，命繼岌兄事之。

translations.literal: On jisi, Zhu Youqian was granted the surname and personal name Li Jilin; the emperor ordered Jiji to treat him as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi the emperor bestowed the name Li Jilin on Zhu Youqian and commanded Li Jiji to honor him as an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 以康延孝為鄭州防禦使，賜姓名曰李紹琛。

translations.literal: Kang Yanxiao was made defense commissioner of Zhengzhou and granted the surname and personal name Li Shaochen.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Yanxiao was appointed defense commissioner of Zhengzhou and given the Tang name Li Shaochen.

sentences.zh: 廢北都，復為成德軍。

translations.literal: The northern capital was abolished and restored as the Chengde army.
translations.idiomatic: The northern capital was abolished and the region reverted to the Chengde command.

sentences.zh: 賜宣武節度使袁象先姓名曰李紹安。

translations.literal: Yuan Xiangxian, military commissioner of Xuanwu, was granted the surname and personal name Li Shao'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiangxian, military commissioner of Xuanwu, received the Tang name Li Shao'an.

sentences.zh: 匡國節度使溫韜入朝，賜姓名曰李紹沖。

translations.literal: Wen Tao, military commissioner of Kuangguo, entered court and was granted the surname and personal name Li Shaochong.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tao of Kuangguo came to court and was given the name Li Shaochong.

sentences.zh: 紹沖多繼金帛賂劉夫人及權貴伶宦，旬日，復遣還鎮。

translations.literal: Shaochong abundantly continued presenting gold and silk to bribe Lady Liu and the powerful, actors, and eunuchs; within ten days he was again dispatched back to his commission.
translations.idiomatic: Shaochong lavished gold and silk on Lady Liu, the great officers, actors, and eunuchs. Within ten days he was sent back to his post.

sentences.zh: 郭崇韜曰：「國家為唐雪恥，溫韜發唐山陵殆遍，其罪與朱溫相埒耳，何得復居方鎮，天下義士其謂我何！」

translations.literal: Guo Chongtao said: "The state avenged Tang's shame—Wen Tao opened Tang imperial tombs nearly throughout; his crime is comparable to Zhu Wen's—how can he again hold a regional commission? What will the realm's men of righteousness say of us!
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao protested: "We restored Tang to avenge its humiliation. Wen Tao plundered nearly every Tang imperial tomb. His crime ranks with Zhu Wen's. How can we send him back to command a region? What will men of honor throughout the realm think of us?

sentences.zh: 上曰：「入汴之初，已赦其罪。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "At the beginning of entering Bian, his crime was already pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "When we first entered Bian we already pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 竟遣之。

translations.literal: In the end he was dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Wen Tao was sent back anyway.

sentences.zh: 戊申，中書奏以：「國用未充，請量留三省、寺、監官，餘並停，俟見任者滿二十五月，以次代之；

translations.literal: On wushen, the chancellery memorialized: "State revenue is not sufficient—we request that offices of the Three Departments, directorates, and supervisorates be retained in measured numbers, the rest all suspended, waiting until incumbents complete twenty-five months, then replacing them in order;
translations.idiomatic: On wushen the chancellery reported: "Treasury income is still short. We ask to retain only a limited roster in the Three Departments and the directorates and supervisorates, suspend all other posts, and fill vacancies only after incumbents have served twenty-five months;

sentences.zh: 其西班上將軍以下，令樞密院准此。」

translations.literal: for the western class from senior generals downward, let the Bureau of Military Affairs follow this standard.
translations.idiomatic: the Bureau of Military Affairs should apply the same rule to military offices from senior generals of the western class downward."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 人頗咨怨。

translations.literal: People were rather resentful in complaint.
translations.idiomatic: There was widespread grumbling among officials.

sentences.zh: 初，梁均王將祀南郊於洛陽，聞楊劉陷而止，其儀物具在。

translations.literal: At the beginning, the Liang Prince of Jun was about to sacrifice at the southern suburbs in Luoyang; hearing Yangliu had fallen, he stopped, but the ritual implements remained fully prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the last Liang emperor had been preparing to offer sacrifice to Heaven at the southern suburbs in Luoyang. When he learned that Yangliu had fallen, he abandoned the rite, though all the ceremonial equipment was still in place.

sentences.zh: 張全義請上亟幸洛陽，謁廟畢即祀南郊；

translations.literal: Zhang Quanyi requested that the emperor urgently visit Luoyang, and that after paying respects at the ancestral temple he at once sacrifice at the southern suburbs;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quanyi urged the emperor to go quickly to Luoyang, perform the temple rites, and then carry out the southern suburbs sacrifice without delay;

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，復以梁東京開封府為宣武軍汴州。

translations.literal: On bingchen, the Liang eastern capital Kaifeng prefecture was again made Xuanwu army Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Kaifeng—the Liang eastern capital—was restored as Bianzhou, seat of the Xuanwu command.

sentences.zh: 梁以宋州為宣武軍，詔更名歸德軍。

translations.literal: The Liang had made Songzhou the Xuanwu army; an edict renamed it the Guide army.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Liang, Songzhou had held the name Xuanwu; an edict now renamed that command the Guide army.

sentences.zh: 詔文武官先詣洛陽。

translations.literal: An edict ordered civil and military officials to proceed first to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commanded civil and military officials to go ahead to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 議者以郭崇韜勳臣為宰相，不能知朝廷典故，當用前朝名家以佐之。

translations.literal: Those in discussion held that Guo Chongtao, a meritorious minister serving as chancellor, could not know the court's established precedents, and that former-dynasty eminent families should be used to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that Guo Chongtao, though a meritorious minister now serving as chancellor, lacked familiarity with court ritual and precedent, and that eminent men of the former dynasty should be appointed to assist him.

sentences.zh: 或薦禮部尚書薛廷珪，太子少保李琪，嘗為太祖冊禮使，皆耆宿有文，宜為相。

translations.literal: Some recommended Minister of Rites Xue Tinggui and Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent Li Qi, who had once served as investiture-ritual envoy for Emperor Taizu—both aged veterans with literary accomplishment, fit to be chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Some recommended Xue Tinggui, Minister of Rites, and Li Qi, Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, both aged men of letters who had once served as investiture envoys under Emperor Taizu and were thought worthy of the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 崇韜奏廷珪浮華無相業，琪傾險無士風；

translations.literal: Chongtao memorialized that Tinggui was flashy and lacked the substance of a chancellor, and Qi was treacherous and lacked the bearing of a gentleman;
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao objected that Tinggui was showy and unfit for high office, and that Qi was scheming and lacked the character of a true scholar-official;

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞趙光胤廉潔方正，自梁未亡，北人皆稱其有宰相器。

translations.literal: Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Zhao Guangyin was incorruptible and upright; since before the Liang had perished, northerners all called him possessed of the capacity of a chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant Director Zhao Guangyin was honest, upright, and widely respected; even before the Liang fell, men in the north had spoken of him as chancellor material.

sentences.zh: 豆盧革薦禮部侍郎韋說諳練朝章。

translations.literal: Doulu Ge recommended Vice Minister of Rites Wei Shuo, thoroughly versed in court regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Doulu Ge recommended Vice Minister of Rites Wei Shuo, who was thoroughly versed in court protocol.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以光胤為中書侍郎，與說並同平章事。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Guangyin was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and, together with Shuo, appointed Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Guangyin was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and, together with Shuo, named Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 光胤，光逢之弟；

translations.literal: Guangyin was Guangfeng's younger brother;
translations.idiomatic: Guangyin was the younger brother of Zhao Guangfeng;

sentences.zh: 說，岫之子；

translations.literal: Shuo was Xiu's son;
translations.idiomatic: Shuo was the son of Wei Xiu;

sentences.zh: 廷珪，逢之子也。

translations.literal: Tinggui was Feng's son.
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui was the son of Zhao Feng.

sentences.zh: 光胤性輕率，喜自矜；

translations.literal: Guangyin's nature was frivolous, and he delighted in self-praise;
translations.idiomatic: Guangyin was light-minded and fond of boasting;

sentences.zh: 說謹重守常而已。

translations.literal: Shuo was merely cautious, grave, and observant of the ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo was merely cautious and steady, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 趙光逢自梁朝罷相，杜門不交賓客，光胤時往見之，語及政事。

translations.literal: Zhao Guangfeng, since being dismissed as chancellor under the Liang, had shut his doors and received no guests; Guangyin would from time to time go to see him and speak of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhao Guangfeng was removed from the chancellorship under the Liang, he shut his doors to visitors. Guangyin still called on him from time to time and talked politics.

sentences.zh: 他日，光逢署其戶曰：「請不言中書事。」

translations.literal: On another day, Guangfeng inscribed on his door: "Please do not speak of Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One day Guangfeng posted a notice on his door that read, "Please do not discuss affairs of the Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 租庸副使孔謙畏張憲公正，欲專使務，言於郭崇韜曰：「東京重地，須大臣鎮之，非張公不可。」

translations.literal: Deputy commissioner of the Rent and Corvée Bureau Kong Qian feared Zhang Xian's fairness and wished to monopolize bureau affairs; he said to Guo Chongtao, "The eastern capital is a vital region and must be garrisoned by a great minister—none but Lord Zhang will do.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Qian, deputy commissioner of the Rent and Corvée Bureau, feared Zhang Xian's integrity and wanted sole control of the bureau. He told Guo Chongtao, "The eastern capital is too important to leave lightly guarded—it must be held by a senior minister, and only Lord Zhang will do.

sentences.zh: 崇韜即奏以憲為東京副留守，知留守事。

translations.literal: Chongtao at once memorialized to appoint Xian eastern-capital deputy regent, with charge of regent affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao promptly memorialized to appoint Xian deputy regent of the eastern capital with full authority over the garrison.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以豆盧革判租庸，兼諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Doulu Ge was assigned to administer the Rent and Corvée Bureau and concurrently made transport commissioner for salt and iron in all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Doulu Ge was put in charge of the Rent and Corvée Bureau and also named transport commissioner for salt and iron across all circuits.

sentences.zh: 謙彌失望。

translations.literal: Qian was all the more disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Qian was bitterly disappointed.

sentences.zh: 己未，加張全義守尚書令，高季興守中書令。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Zhang Quanyi was promoted to acting Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Gao Jixing to acting Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Zhang Quanyi was promoted to acting Director of the Department of State Affairs and Gao Jixing to acting Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時季興入朝，上待之甚厚，從容問曰：「朕欲用兵於吳、蜀，二國何先？」

translations.literal: At this time Jixing had come to court; the emperor treated him very generously and, at leisure, asked, "I wish to use troops against Wu and Shu—which of the two states should come first?
translations.idiomatic: Jixing was then at court, and the emperor received him with great favor. In an unhurried tone he asked, "I mean to campaign against Wu and Shu—which should I strike first?

sentences.zh: 季興以蜀道險難取，乃對曰：「吳地薄民貧，克之無益，不如先伐蜀。

translations.literal: Jixing, because the Shu road was perilous and hard to take, therefore replied, "Wu has thin soil and impoverished people; conquering it would be of no benefit—it would be better first to attack Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing how treacherous the road into Shu was, Jixing answered, "Wu is poor in land and people. Conquering it would gain you little. You would do better to attack Shu first.

sentences.zh: 蜀土富饒，又主荒民怨，伐之必克。

translations.literal: Shu's land is rich and fertile, and moreover its ruler is dissolute while the people resent him—attacking it will surely succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Shu is rich, its ruler idle, and its people resentful. A campaign there is sure to succeed.

sentences.zh: 克蜀之後，順流而下，取吳如反掌耳。」

translations.literal: After Shu is taken, going downstream, taking Wu will be like turning over the palm.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shu falls, you can sweep downriver and seize Wu as easily as turning over your hand.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「善！」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Excellent!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Well said!"

sentences.zh: 辛酉，復以永平軍大安府為西京京兆府。

translations.literal: On xinyou, the Yongping army's Da'an prefecture was again made the western capital Jingzhao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou Da'an—the seat of the Yongping command—was restored as Jingzhao prefecture, capital of the western capital.

sentences.zh: 甲子，帝發大梁；

translations.literal: On jiazi, the emperor set out from Daliang;
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the emperor departed Daliang;

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚午，至洛陽。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on gengwu, he reached Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on gengwu, he arrived at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 吳越王鏐以行軍司馬杜建徽為左丞相。

translations.literal: King Qian Liu of Wuyue made campaigning marshal Du Jianhui left chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: King Qian Liu of Wuyue appointed campaigning marshal Du Jianhui left chief minister.

sentences.zh: 壬申，詔以汴州宮苑為行宮。

translations.literal: On renshen, an edict made the Bianzhou palace park a traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen an edict designated the Bianzhou palace grounds as an imperial traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 以耀州為順義軍，延州為彰武軍，鄧州為威勝軍，晉州為建雄軍，安州為安遠軍；

translations.literal: Yaozhou was made the Shunyi army, Yanzhou the Zhangwu army, Dengzhou the Weisheng army, Jinzhou the Jianxiong army, and Anzhou the Anyuan army;
translations.idiomatic: Yaozhou was renamed the Shunyi command, Yanzhou the Zhangwu command, Dengzhou the Weisheng command, Jinzhou the Jianxiong command, and Anzhou the Anyuan command;

sentences.zh: 自餘籓鎮，皆復唐舊名。

translations.literal: as for the remaining regional commands, all restored Tang's old names.
translations.idiomatic: all other regional commands likewise reverted to their Tang-era names.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，御史台奏：「朱溫篡逆，刪改本朝《律令格式》，悉收舊本焚之，今台司及刑部、大理寺所用皆偽廷之法。

translations.literal: On gengchen, the Censorate memorialized: "Zhu Wen usurped and rebelled, revised and altered this dynasty's Statutes, Ordinances, Decrees, and Formats, gathered all old copies and burned them—today the Censorate, Ministry of Justice, and Court of Judicial Review all use the false court's laws.
