translations.idiomatic: On gengchen the Censorate reported: "When Zhu Wen seized power he revised the Tang Statutes, Ordinances, Decrees, and Formats, collected every old copy, and burned them. The Censorate, Ministry of Justice, and Court of Judicial Review now all rely on the spurious code of the usurping court.

sentences.zh: 聞定州敕庫獨有本朝《律令格式》具在，乞下本道錄進。」

translations.literal: It is heard that Dingzhou's edict archive alone has this dynasty's Statutes, Ordinances, Decrees, and Formats complete; we beg that the circuit be ordered to copy and submit them.
translations.idiomatic: We have learned that the edict archive at Dingzhou alone still holds a complete set of the Tang code. We ask that the circuit be ordered to copy and submit it.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the request.

sentences.zh: 李繼韜聞上滅梁，憂懼，不知所為，欲北走契丹，會有詔征詣闕；

translations.literal: Li Jitao, hearing the emperor had destroyed the Liang, was anxious and afraid and did not know what to do; he wished to flee north to the Khitan, when there came an edict summoning him to court;
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jitao learned that the emperor had overthrown the Liang, he was stricken with fear and did not know what to do. He was about to flee north to the Khitan when an edict arrived summoning him to court;

sentences.zh: 繼韜將行，其弟繼遠曰：「兄以反為名，何地自容！

translations.literal: As Jitao was about to depart, his younger brother Jiyuan said, "Elder brother, you are known as a rebel—where can you find a place for yourself!
translations.idiomatic: As Jitao prepared to leave, his younger brother Jiyuan said, "Brother, you are already branded a rebel. Where in the world can you hide!

sentences.zh: 往與不往等耳，不若深溝高壘，坐食積粟，猶可延歲月；

translations.literal: Going or not going are the same; better to dig deep moats and raise high ramparts, sit and consume stored grain—you can still prolong months;
translations.idiomatic: Whether you go or stay makes no difference. Better to dig deep moats, raise high walls, and live off your stored grain—you might still buy yourself some time;

sentences.zh: 入朝，立死矣。」

translations.literal: If you enter court, you will die at once.
translations.idiomatic: Go to court and you will be killed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 或謂繼韜曰：「先令公有大功於國，主上於公，季父也，往必無虞。」

translations.literal: Someone said to Jitao, "Your late father performed great service to the state; the sovereign, toward you, is like a father's younger brother—if you go, there will surely be no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Others told Jitao, "Your father rendered great service to the state. The emperor treats you as a nephew. If you go, you have nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 繼韜母楊氏，善蓄財，家貲百萬，乃與楊氏偕行，繼銀四十萬兩，他貨稱是，大布賂遺。

translations.literal: Jitao's mother, Lady Yang, was skilled at amassing wealth—the family fortune was a million; he therefore traveled together with Lady Yang, continuing four hundred thousand taels of silver and other goods in like measure, broadly distributing bribes and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Jitao's mother, Lady Yang, was a shrewd hoarder of wealth; the family fortune ran to a million strings of cash. Jitao set out with her, bringing four hundred thousand taels of silver and gifts in proportion, and lavished bribes on all sides.

sentences.zh: 伶人宦官爭為之言曰：「繼韜初無邪謀，為奸人所惑耳。

translations.literal: Actors and eunuchs vied to speak for him, saying, "Jitao at first had no wicked plot—he was merely misled by evil men.
translations.idiomatic: Actors and eunuchs all pleaded on his behalf, saying, "Jitao never harbored treason. Evil men led him astray.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭親賢，不可無後。」

translations.literal: Sizhao was close kin and worthy—the line must not be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao was a loyal kinsman and a worthy man. His house must not die out.

sentences.zh: 楊氏復入宮見帝，泣請其死，以其先人為言；

translations.literal: Lady Yang again entered the palace to see the emperor, weeping and begging for his life, speaking in terms of their forebears;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang went again into the palace to see the emperor, weeping and begging for his life and invoking the deeds of his ancestors;

sentences.zh: 又求哀於劉夫人，劉夫人亦為之言。

translations.literal: She also pleaded for mercy from Lady Liu, and Lady Liu too spoke on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: She also appealed to Lady Liu, who likewise interceded for him.

sentences.zh: 及繼韜入見待罪，上釋之，留月餘，屢從游畋，寵待如故。

translations.literal: When Jitao entered audience to await punishment, the emperor released him; he remained over a month, repeatedly accompanying him in outings and hunts, favored and treated as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Jitao came to court to submit to judgment, the emperor pardoned him. He stayed more than a month, often joined the emperor on hunts and excursions, and was favored as before.

sentences.zh: 皇弟義成節度使、同平章事存渥深詆訶之，繼韜心不自安，復賂左右求還鎮，上不許。

translations.literal: The emperor's younger brother, Yicheng military commissioner and Grand Councilor Cunwo, deeply reviled him; Jitao's heart was not at ease, and he again bribed those around the throne seeking return to his commission—the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's younger brother Li Cunwo, military commissioner of Yicheng and Grand Councilor, denounced him harshly. Jitao grew uneasy and again bribed the emperor's attendants to let him return to his post, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 繼韜潛遣人遺繼遠書，教軍士縱火，冀天子復遣己撫安之，事洩，辛巳，貶登州長史，尋斬於天津橋南，並其二子。

translations.literal: Jitao secretly sent a man to deliver a letter to Jiyuan, instructing the soldiers to set fires, hoping the Son of Heaven would again dispatch him to pacify and reassure them; the affair leaked out—on xinsi he was demoted to secretary of Dengzhou, and soon afterward executed south of Tianjin Bridge, together with his two sons.
translations.idiomatic: Jitao secretly sent word to Jiyuan urging the garrison to set fires, hoping the emperor would send him back to restore order. When the plot was exposed, on xinsi he was demoted to secretary of Dengzhou and soon executed south of Tianjin Bridge along with his two sons.

sentences.zh: 遣使斬繼遠於上黨，以李繼達充軍城巡檢。

translations.literal: An envoy was dispatched to behead Jiyuan at Shangdang; Li Jida was appointed to fill the post of garrison patrol inspector.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy was sent to execute Jiyuan at Shangdang, and Li Jida was appointed garrison patrol inspector.

sentences.zh: 召權知軍州事李繼儔詣闕，繼儔據有繼韜之室，料簡妓妾，搜校貨財，不時即路。

translations.literal: Acting prefect of the army and prefecture Li Jichou was summoned to court; Jichou seized Jitao's residence, sorted through singing girls and concubines, searched out goods and wealth, and did not set out on the road in timely fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jichou, acting prefect of the command, was summoned to court. He seized Jitao's house, sorted through his concubines, inventoried his wealth, and delayed his departure.

sentences.zh: 繼達怒曰：「吾家兄弟父子同時誅死者四人，大兄曾無骨肉之情，貪淫如此；

translations.literal: Jida angrily said, "In our family, four brothers, fathers, and sons were executed at the same time, yet the elder brother never showed the feeling of flesh and bone—greedy and licentious to this degree;
translations.idiomatic: Jida raged, "Four men of our house—brothers, fathers, and sons—were put to death together, yet our eldest brother showed not a shred of kinship feeling. Instead he grows greedy and debauched;

sentences.zh: 吾誠羞之，無面視人，生不如死！」

translations.literal: I am truly ashamed of him—I have no face to look upon others; living is not as good as dying!
translations.idiomatic: I am ashamed to call him kin. I have no face left to show the world. Better dead than alive!

sentences.zh: 甲申，繼達衰服，帥麾下百騎坐戟門呼曰：「誰與吾反者？」

translations.literal: On jiashen, Jida in mourning garments led a hundred riders of his command, seated at the halberd gate, and shouted, "Who will rebel with me?
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Jida, dressed in mourning, led a hundred horsemen to the halberd gate and cried out, "Who will rise with me?

sentences.zh: 因攻牙宅，斬繼儔。

translations.literal: He then attacked the headquarters residence and beheaded Jichou.
translations.idiomatic: He then stormed the headquarters residence and killed Jichou.

sentences.zh: 節度副使李繼珂聞亂，募市人，得千餘，攻子城。

translations.literal: Deputy military commissioner Li Jike, hearing of the disturbance, recruited townspeople and got more than a thousand, attacking the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy military commissioner Li Jike, hearing of the revolt, raised more than a thousand townspeople and assaulted the inner city.

sentences.zh: 繼達知事不濟，開東門，歸私第，盡殺其妻子，將奔契丹，出城數里，從騎皆散，乃自剄。

translations.literal: Jida, knowing the affair would not succeed, opened the eastern gate, returned to his private residence, killed all his wife and children, and was about to flee to the Khitan; several li outside the city his accompanying riders all dispersed, and he then cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the revolt had failed, Jida opened the eastern gate, returned home, killed his wife and children, and tried to flee to the Khitan. A few li outside the walls his followers melted away, and he cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 甲申，吳王復遣司農卿洛陽盧蘋來奉使，嚴可求豫料帝所問，教蘋應對，既至，皆如可求所料。

translations.literal: On jiashen, the King of Wu again dispatched Minister of Agriculture Lu Pin of Luoyang to come on embassy; Yan Keqiu beforehand anticipated what the emperor would ask and instructed Pin in his replies—once he arrived, all was as Keqiu had anticipated.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen the King of Wu again sent Lu Pin of Luoyang, Minister of Agriculture, as envoy. Yan Keqiu anticipated every question the emperor would ask and coached Pin in his answers. When Pin arrived, events unfolded exactly as Keqiu had predicted.

sentences.zh: 蘋還，言唐主荒於游畋，嗇財拒諫，內外皆怨。

translations.literal: Pin returned and reported that the Tang ruler was dissolute in outings and hunting, stingy with wealth and rejecting remonstrance—within and without, all resented him.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Pin reported that the Tang emperor was idle with hunting, tight-fisted, deaf to remonstrance, and resented by court and country alike.

sentences.zh: 高季興在洛陽，帝左右伶宦求貨無厭，季興忿之。

translations.literal: Gao Jixing was in Luoyang; the actors and eunuchs around the emperor sought goods without satiety, and Jixing resented them.
translations.idiomatic: While Gao Jixing was in Luoyang, the actors and eunuchs around the emperor demanded gifts without end, and Jixing grew furious.

sentences.zh: 帝欲留季興，郭崇韜諫曰：「陛下新得天下，諸侯不過遣子弟將佐入貢，惟高季興身自入朝，當褒賞以勸來者；

translations.literal: The emperor wished to detain Jixing; Guo Chongtao remonstrated, saying, "Your Majesty has newly obtained the realm—of the feudal lords none but send sons, younger brothers, generals, and aides to offer tribute; only Gao Jixing came to court in person—he should be praised and rewarded to encourage those who come afterward;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to keep Jixing at court. Guo Chongtao advised, "Your Majesty has only just won the realm. Most lords send sons, brothers, or officers with tribute. Gao Jixing came in person. He should be honored and rewarded to encourage others to follow;

sentences.zh: 乃羈留不遣，棄信虧義，沮四海之心，非計也。」

translations.literal: yet to detain and not release him abandons trust and damages righteousness, discouraging the hearts of the four seas—it is no plan.
translations.idiomatic: To hold him against his will would break faith, violate justice, and chill the loyalty of the realm. That is no wise policy.

sentences.zh: 乃遣之。

translations.literal: He was then dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then let him go.

sentences.zh: 季興倍道而去，至許州，謂左右曰：「此行有二失：來朝一失，縱我去一失。」

translations.literal: Jixing traveled by double stages and departed; reaching Xuzhou, he said to those around him, "This journey had two errors: coming to court was one error, and letting me go was another error.
translations.idiomatic: Jixing fled by forced marches. At Xuzhou he told his attendants, "This trip revealed two blunders: letting me come to court was one, and letting me leave was another.

sentences.zh: 過襄州，節度使孔勍留宴，中夜，斬關而去。

translations.literal: Passing Xiangzhou, military commissioner Kong Qing detained him for a banquet; in the middle of the night he broke through the pass and left.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Xiangzhou, military commissioner Kong Qing kept him for a banquet. At midnight Jixing broke through the gate and fled.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，至江陵，握梁震手曰：「不用君言，幾不免虎口。」

translations.literal: On dingyou, reaching Jiangling, he grasped Liang Zhen's hand and said, "Had I not used your words, I would nearly have escaped the tiger's maw.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, reaching Jiangling, he took Liang Zhen's hand and said, "Had I not heeded your counsel, I would barely have escaped the tiger's jaws.

sentences.zh: 又謂將佐曰：「新朝百戰方得河南，乃對功臣舉手去，『吾於十指上得天下，』矜伐如此，則他人皆無功矣，其誰不解體！

translations.literal: He also said to his generals and aides, "The new court fought a hundred battles before obtaining Henan, yet toward meritorious ministers it raised its hand and said, 'I obtained the realm on my ten fingers'—boasting so, then all others have no achievement; who will not lose heart!
translations.idiomatic: He also told his officers, "The new dynasty won Henan only after a hundred battles, yet the emperor waved his fingers at his ministers and said, 'I won the realm on these ten fingers.' With such boasting, every other man is rendered worthless. Who would not lose heart!

sentences.zh: 又荒於禽色，何能久長！

translations.literal: Moreover he is dissolute in birds and women—how can he long endure!
translations.idiomatic: He is idle with hunting and women. How can such a reign last!

sentences.zh: 吾無憂矣。」

translations.literal: I have no worries.
translations.idiomatic: I have nothing left to fear.

sentences.zh: 乃繕城積粟，招納梁舊兵，為戰守之備。

translations.literal: He then repaired the walls, stored grain, recruited and received old Liang soldiers, and made preparations for war and defense.
translations.idiomatic: He then repaired his walls, stockpiled grain, recruited former Liang soldiers, and prepared for war and siege.
